## Overview

Package kit provides styled components for Tela apps: a button, a card, a text field, in the look of shadcn/ui (style "new-york-v4", at the registry commit [`ShadcnCommit`](#constants)), built on the behavior hooks of package aria and the classes of package h. It is the layer an app is written with; reach for aria and h when a component of the kit does not fit.

### The shape of a component

Every component is a struct component (ARCHITECTURE ADR-088): its props are the fields of the struct, and Build returns its element.

```go
kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Size: kit.Sm, OnClick: save, Children: h.Text("Save")}
```

Every component has the same few fields, with the same meaning:

- Class is added to the classes of the root element after the component's own, and Tela's class order is last-wins, so Class overrides the look with no merging: Class: "w-full" widens a Card, Class: "rounded-full" rounds a Button.
- Props is a tela.Child with more props for the root element, such as h.Key, h.TestID or h.OnMouseEnter(...). It takes one value: merge several with tela.MergeProps(h.TestID("save"), h.OnMouseEnter(warm)).
- Children is a tela.Component, the content of the component. A component with several parts has a slot for each as a tela.Component field (kit.Card has Title, Description, Action, Children and Footer); nil leaves a slot out. A slot that is only text for assistive technologies, such as a Field's Label, Description and Error, is a string. The Class of a part is named after it: HeaderClass, FooterClass.
- Behavior fields are named after the HTML or React prop they stand for: Disabled, OnClick, Type, Placeholder, Name, ID, ReadOnly, AutoFocus, MaxLength. Variant and Size choose among the looks of the recipe.
- Icons are slots: every icon a component draws is a tela.Icon field (Button.Icon and IconEnd, Badge.Icon), so an app uses the icon set it likes, such as icons/lucide. Where shadcn draws an icon itself, the field has Lucide's as its default (the X of Dialog.CloseIcon).

Because a struct component compares its fields to skip a build, a component given a func (OnClick) or a slice builds on every parent build; that is cheap, and tela.Callback makes it skippable when it matters.

### Controlled and uncontrolled

A component that has a value follows one rule (ADR-101), whatever the value is. Give a pointer to your state to control it, a default to leave it to the component, and a callback to be told of changes:

```go
name, setName := tela.UseState("")
kit.Input{Value: &name, OnValueChange: setName.Set} // controlled
kit.Input{DefaultValue: "Ana"}                      // uncontrolled
```

The same names recur: Value/DefaultValue/OnValueChange for a string, Checked (\*bool)/DefaultChecked/OnCheckedChange for an on/off control, Open (\*bool)/DefaultOpen/OnOpenChange for what opens and closes. A control that holds a choice among keys takes Value \*K, DefaultValue \*K and OnValueChange func(K).

A DefaultValue is a pointer when the zero value of its type is a valid value, so that "no default" and "the zero value" differ: a choice among keys (the int 0 can be a tab), a slider (0 can be where it starts) and a color (the zero Color is transparent black) take new(...) of the value (kit.Tabs\[int\]{DefaultValue: new(0)}), and nil leaves the choice to the component. Where the zero value means "none" it stays a value: a string, an aria.Date, an aria.DateRange.

### Customization, in three levels

1\. Theme tokens. [`Theme`](#func-theme) is shadcn's neutral theme with a 10 px radius; change its colors and every component follows (bg-primary, text-muted-foreground and the other classes of the recipes are tokens):

```go
theme := kit.Theme()
theme.Colors["primary"] = tela.SchemeColor{Light: tela.Hex("#4f46e5"), Dark: tela.Hex("#818cf8")}
tela.Main(tela.App{Title: "Notes", Root: Notes{}, Theme: &theme,
    RootClass: "bg-background text-foreground"})
```

2\. Recipes. The whole look of a component is data: a [`Style`](#type-style) has one struct of class strings per component (ButtonStyle, CardStyle...), with a Root for the root element and a field for each other part, variant and size. [`DefaultStyle`](#func-defaultstyle) returns a copy of the defaults to edit and [`StyleProvider`](#type-styleprovider) applies the edited one to a subtree, as h.Scheme does for the color scheme:

```go
s := kit.DefaultStyle()
s.Card.Root += " backdrop-blur-xl"
s.Button.Variants["glass"] = "bg-white/10 text-white hover:bg-white/20"
return kit.StyleProvider{Style: &s, Children: Dashboard{}}
```

A Variant or Size is valid when the active recipe defines it, so "glass" above is a variant of every Button under the provider. One the recipe does not define panics in dev mode, naming the ones it does and the closest, and uses the default look otherwise. Components of your own read the active style with [`UseStyle`](#func-usestyle). Build a style once and do not edit it after giving it to a provider.

3\. Per instance. Class, the Class of a part, Props and the icon slots change one component:

```go
kit.Card{Class: "w-full max-w-sm", HeaderClass: "pb-6 border-b", TitleLevel: 2, Title: h.Text("Billing")}
```

### What is there

Button, Badge, Card, Avatar, Label, Input, Textarea, Separator, Skeleton, Field, FieldSet, Select, Tabs, Table and Toaster; the overlays Dialog, AlertDialog, Popover and Tooltip; the menus DropdownMenu, Menubar and ContextMenu; and the controls that choose: Checkbox, Switch, RadioGroup, Toggle, ToggleGroup (the segmented control), Slider and Progress; and the dates: Calendar, RangeCalendar, DatePicker and DateRangePicker. A [`ColorPicker`](#type-colorpicker) chooses a [`tela.Color`](API-Reference-tela#type-color) with an area for the saturation and brightness, a hue slider, an optional alpha slider, a hex field and optional swatches; a [`ColorInput`](#type-colorinput) is the same behind a button that shows the color (the look of both is the kit's own, shadcn/ui has no color picker):

```go
kit.ColorPicker{Value: &color, OnValueChange: setColor.Set, Alpha: true,
    Swatches: []tela.Color{tela.Hex("#ef4444"), tela.Hex("#22c55e")}}
kit.ColorInput{DefaultValue: new(tela.Hex("#6366f1")), OnValueCommit: save}
```

A [`Table`](#type-table) shows rows of any type through columns, sorts by a header (aria-sort, Enter and Space) and keeps its header and leading columns in place when it scrolls:

```go
kit.Table[Invoice]{Rows: invoices, RowKey: func(i Invoice) any { return i.ID },
    Columns: []kit.Column[Invoice]{
        {Header: "Invoice", Cell: func(i Invoice) tela.Node { return h.Text(i.ID) }, Sticky: true, Width: "120px",
            Sort: func(a, b Invoice) int { return strings.Compare(a.ID, b.ID) }},
        {Header: "Amount", Align: kit.AlignRight, Cell: showAmount, Sort: byAmount},
    }}
```

A [`Calendar`](#type-calendar) chooses a date and a [`RangeCalendar`](#type-rangecalendar) a span (the aria.Date and aria.DateRange of package aria, comparable days with no time or zone; the zero value is none), with limits (Min, Max, IsDateUnavailable), several months and the names, digits, first weekday and direction of the locale. A [`DatePicker`](#type-datepicker) and a [`DateRangePicker`](#type-daterangepicker) are shadcn's date picker: an outline button showing the date that opens a popover with the calendar and closes when the date, or the range, is chosen:

```go
day, setDay := tela.UseState(aria.Date{})
kit.DatePicker{Value: &day, OnValueChange: setDay.Set, Min: aria.Today()}
```

A [`Field`](#type-field) is the usual way to put a label, a control, help text and an error together: it ties them with an id, so the label names the control and clicking it focuses the control, and the control is described by the error or the help text. Input, Textarea, Select, DatePicker, DateRangePicker, ColorInput, Checkbox and Switch take the field's id; a ColorPicker gives it to its hex field.

```go
kit.Field{Label: "Email", Description: "We never share it.", Error: errs.Email,
    Children: kit.Input{Type: "email", Value: &email, OnValueChange: setEmail.Set}}
```

A horizontal Field puts the control first; ControlAfter puts it after the text, as in a row of switches. A [`FieldSet`](#type-fieldset) captions a group of controls with a legend and names a RadioGroup or ToggleGroup inside it:

```go
kit.FieldSet{Legend: "Theme", Children: kit.RadioGroup[string]{Items: themes}}
```

### Right to left

The recipes of the kit are written with logical utilities (ps-\*, pe-\*, start-\*, end-\*, ms-\*, me-\*, rounded-s-\*, rounded-e-\*, text-start, text-end) and the rtl: variant, which are the physical ones in left-to-right and mirror under h.Dir("rtl"), so a kit page needs nothing but the direction to be mirrored: menu check marks and shortcuts, a select's items, a dialog's close button, a switch's thumb, a table's sticky columns, a progress bar's fill. What stays physical is a position that names a side (a Toaster's ToastBottomRight, a Popover's Placement "right"), as sonner's and Floating UI's do; an Align of "start" follows the direction.

The components whose arrow keys or drag follow the direction (Slider, Tabs, ToggleGroup, RadioGroup, Menubar, ColorPicker, ColorInput and the calendars) read it at their position with tela.UseDirection, so an h.Dir around the app is all a right-to-left page needs: in it ArrowLeft goes to the next item and a slider's minimum is at the right.

```go
f := i18n.UseFormatter()
return h.Div(h.Dir(f.Dir().String()), App{})
```

Each of them also has a Direction field ("ltr" or "rtl"), which wins over the direction at its position and sets h.Dir on its root, for a component whose direction differs from its surroundings (a calendar has its Locale too).

### Overlays and triggers

A [`Dialog`](#type-dialog), [`AlertDialog`](#type-alertdialog), [`Popover`](#type-popover) and [`Tooltip`](#type-tooltip) draw in a Portal over the window, exist only while they are open (so what is inside them starts afresh each time) and enter and leave with a transition. Each has a Trigger slot, the element that opens it, and the Open (\*bool), DefaultOpen and OnOpenChange of the controlled and uncontrolled rule.

```go
kit.Dialog{
    Trigger:     kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Children: h.Text("Edit profile")},
    Title:       h.Text("Edit profile"),
    Description: h.Text("Make changes to your profile here."),
    Children:    form,
    Footer:      kit.Button{Children: h.Text("Save changes")},
}
```

One rule makes every trigger slot of the kit work, Radix's asChild: the overlay needs to put props on the element that opens it (the press, the aria-expanded and aria-controls, the ref it is placed against, the hover of a tooltip), and it does not wrap the trigger in an element of its own. A trigger slot is a [`Trigger`](#type-trigger), a component with one method, WithTriggerProps(tela.Prop) tela.Component, that merges the props into its root element. [`Button`](#type-button) is a Trigger, as are the kit components that say so; a component of your own becomes one by adding the method; and any other element is made one with [`TriggerFunc`](#type-triggerfunc), which hands you the props to put where you like:

```go
kit.Tooltip{
    Trigger: kit.TriggerFunc(func(p tela.Prop) tela.Node {
        return h.Button(p, h.Class("rounded-full"), h.Text("Docs"))
    }),
    Content: h.Text("Open the manual"),
}
```

A dialog is modal: the page is inert, Tab stays inside, Escape and a press on the scrim close it, and the focus returns to the trigger. An alert dialog is the same for a question that needs an answer, and is not closed by a press outside. A popover is not modal and closes when the focus or a press goes elsewhere. A tooltip opens on hover or keyboard focus and describes its trigger; the tooltips of a window are a group, so after one opened the next opens at once.

A [`Select`](#type-select) and a [`Tabs`](#type-tabs) take their items as slices of structs, generic over the key type, and follow the value rule:

```go
kit.Select[string]{Placeholder: "Select a fruit", Items: []kit.SelectItem[string]{
    {Value: "apple", Label: "Apple"}, {Value: "banana", Label: "Banana"}}}
kit.Tabs[string]{Tabs: []kit.Tab[string]{
    {Value: "account", Label: "Account", Content: AccountForm{}},
    {Value: "password", Label: "Password", Content: PasswordForm{}}}}
```

Toasts have no component to place: a [`Toaster`](#type-toaster) goes once around the app, and any component below it gets a handle with [`UseToast`](#func-usetoast) and shows toasts with it, from a handler or from any goroutine (the handle is comparable and every method is safe to call from any goroutine; there is no global):

```go
tela.Main(tela.App{Title: "Notes", Root: kit.Toaster{Children: Notes{}}})

toast := kit.UseToast()
id := toast.Loading("Uploading…")
go func() { upload(); toast.Success("Uploaded", kit.ToastReplace(id)) }()
```

### Menus

A [`DropdownMenu`](#type-dropdownmenu) (opens from a button), a [`Menubar`](#type-menubar) (a row of menus) and a [`ContextMenu`](#type-contextmenu) (opens on a right click inside an area) are built on the same model of items, [`MenuItem`](#type-menuitem), and draw the same panel. A menu is a slice of items of a kind: a plain item (a label, an icon, a shortcut that is only shown, a destructive variant, OnSelect), a checkbox item, a radio group, a label, a separator or a group; every item that can be chosen has a Key, and the menu's OnSelect reports the key of a plain item:

```go
kit.DropdownMenu[string]{
    Trigger: kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Children: h.Text("Account")},
    Align:   "start",
    Items: []kit.MenuItem[string]{
        {Kind: kit.MenuLabel, Label: "My account"},
        {Key: "profile", Label: "Profile", Shortcut: "⇧⌘P"},
        {Kind: kit.MenuCheckbox, Key: "bars", Label: "Status bar", DefaultChecked: true},
        {Kind: kit.MenuSeparator},
        {Key: "logout", Label: "Log out", Variant: kit.Destructive},
    },
    OnSelect: func(key string) { run(key) },
}
```

The checkbox items and radio groups follow the value rule (Checked and OnCheckedChange, Value and OnValueChange, or a default), and an uncontrolled state is kept by the component, so it outlives the menu closing. Choosing an item closes the menu, as Radix's does, unless the item has KeepOpen. There are no submenus yet: a menu is one level (ADR-141).

### The look and its tests

The class strings are shadcn/ui's own, from the pinned commit [`ShadcnCommit`](#constants), with the translations Tela needs: data-\[state=...\]: is checked: or an aria-\*: variant, \[\&\_svg\]: classes are on the icon slot, a has-\[\>svg\]: padding is a Go condition, and a border with no color (shadcn sets the border color of every element in its base layer) is border-border. Every component has a golden image in light and dark at scales 1 and 2 in testdata, and a page in testdata/chromium written with shadcn's markup, rendered by Chromium with Tailwind 4.3.3, which the tests compare with Tela's rendering: boxes to a few hundredths of a pixel and the pixels to the anti-aliasing of text. The color picker has no shadcn original: its gradients are compared with Chromium's CSS gradients of the same colors, and the rest is checked by goldens and behavior tests.

## Constants

```go
const NoOffset float32 = -1
```

NoOffset as the Offset of a [`Popover`](#type-popover) puts the panel against its trigger: the zero value stands for shadcn's default of 4 px.

```go
const ShadcnCommit = "617134d5810bba521803b3ed787190bacbb80b35"
```

ShadcnCommit is the commit of github.com/shadcn-ui/ui (branch main) whose registry style "new-york-v4" (apps/v4/registry/new-york-v4/ui) the class strings of this package were ported from, and that the Chromium conformance pages in testdata/chromium are written against. Every component of the package follows this one commit (ADR-130).

```go
const ToastForever time.Duration = -1
```

ToastForever as a duration keeps a toast until it is dismissed.

## Functions

### func Theme

```go
func Theme() tela.Theme
```

Theme returns the theme of the kit's look: shadcn/ui's neutral colors with a base radius of 10 px (shadcn's 0.625rem). It is [`tela.DefaultTheme`](API-Reference-tela#func-defaulttheme) with the radius shadcn's components were designed for, so the rounded-md, rounded-lg and rounded-xl of the recipes come out as 8, 10 and 14 px.

```go
theme := kit.Theme()
tela.Main(tela.App{Title: "Notes", Root: Notes{}, Theme: &theme,
    RootClass: "bg-background text-foreground"})
```

Change the tokens on the returned value (theme.Colors\["primary"\] = ...) to restyle every component at once; see [`DefaultStyle`](#func-defaultstyle) to restyle one.

## Types

### type AlertDialog

```go
type AlertDialog struct {
    // Trigger is the element that opens the dialog; nil for a dialog
    // opened only by its state.
    Trigger Trigger
    // Title and Description are the question and its explanation; both name
    // the dialog for assistive technologies.
    Title, Description tela.Component
    // Cancel and Action are the labels of the buttons.
    Cancel, Action tela.Component
    // Destructive gives the Action button the destructive variant.
    Destructive bool
    // OnAction and OnCancel are called when the Action or Cancel button is
    // pressed, before the dialog closes.
    OnAction, OnCancel func()
    // Size is the default or Sm, a narrow dialog with the buttons in two
    // equal columns and centered text.
    Size Size

    // Open points to the open state of a controlled dialog; nil leaves the
    // state to the dialog, which starts closed unless DefaultOpen is set.
    Open         *bool
    DefaultOpen  bool
    OnOpenChange func(open bool)
    // Disabled disables the trigger, which is then inert and dimmed by its
    // recipe; the dialog does not open. Set it here: the trigger props
    // override a Disabled given to the trigger component itself.
    Disabled bool

    // Class is added after the recipe's Root classes, to the panel. The
    // other Class fields do the same for their part.
    Class            string
    OverlayClass     string
    HeaderClass      string
    TitleClass       string
    DescriptionClass string
    FooterClass      string
    CancelClass      string
    ActionClass      string
    // Props are more props for the dialog element (the panel).
    Props tela.Child
}
```

AlertDialog is a modal dialog that interrupts the user with a question that needs an answer, shadcn/ui's AlertDialog: a title, a description and two buttons, Cancel and Action. It has the alertdialog role, takes the focus on its first button (Cancel, so that Enter never confirms by accident), and, unlike a [`Dialog`](#type-dialog), is not closed by a press on the scrim: only the buttons and Escape close it.

```go
kit.AlertDialog{
    Trigger:     kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Children: h.Text("Delete project")},
    Title:       h.Text("Are you absolutely sure?"),
    Description: h.Text("This action cannot be undone. The project and its deployments are deleted."),
    Action:      h.Text("Delete"),
    Destructive: true,
    OnAction:    deleteProject,
}
```

Cancel and Action are the labels of the two buttons ("Cancel" and "Continue" when nil); a slot may be any component, such as a label with an icon. The buttons are \[Button\]s: Action is the default variant, or Destructive with Destructive set, and Cancel is the outline variant; ActionClass and CancelClass add classes to them. Both close the dialog; OnAction and OnCancel say which was chosen. Escape closes it as Cancel does, without calling OnCancel.

The Trigger slot is a [`Trigger`](#type-trigger). Open, DefaultOpen and OnOpenChange are the usual controlled and uncontrolled pair.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
deleted := false
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"), kit.AlertDialog{
        Trigger:     kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Children: h.Text("Delete project")},
        Title:       h.Text("Are you absolutely sure?"),
        Description: h.Text("This action cannot be undone."),
        Action:      h.Text("Delete"),
        Destructive: true,
        OnAction:    func() { deleted = true },
    })
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Delete project"))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Delete"))
fmt.Println("deleted:", deleted)
// Output: deleted: true
```

### type Button

```go
type Button struct {
    // Variant is the look: Default, Secondary, Outline, Ghost, Destructive
    // or Link.
    Variant Variant
    // Size is Default, Xs, Sm, Lg, Icon, IconXs, IconSm or IconLg.
    Size Size
    // Type is "button", "submit" or "reset" (h.Type). Empty leaves the
    // element's default: "submit" inside an h.Form, else "button".
    Type string
    // Disabled makes the button inert (h.Disabled) and dims it.
    Disabled bool
    // OnClick is called when the button is clicked or activated with the
    // keyboard.
    OnClick func()
    // AriaLabel names a button whose content is not text, such as an icon
    // button.
    AriaLabel string
    // Icon is drawn before the children, IconEnd after them. Their size
    // and shape come from the recipe's Icon and IconSizes.
    Icon, IconEnd tela.Icon
    // Children is the label.
    Children tela.Component
    // Class is added after the recipe's classes, so it wins over them.
    Class string
    // Props are more props for the button element: a Key, a TestID, a
    // handler.
    Props tela.Child
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Button is a button, shadcn/ui's Button: the rounded, medium-weight control in six variants and eight sizes. It is an h.Button, so it takes focus with Tab, is activated with Enter and Space, shows hover and active states, and inside an h.Form submits it (Type "submit" is the HTML default there).

```go
kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Size: kit.Sm, OnClick: save, Children: h.Text("Save")}

// An icon before the label (your own tela.Icon), and an icon-only button.
kit.Button{Icon: lucide.Mail, Children: h.Text("Login with email")}
kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Size: kit.Icon, Icon: lucide.ChevronRight, AriaLabel: "Next"}
```

A Variant or Size the active [`Style`](#type-style) does not define panics in dev mode with the closest one.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
saved := 0
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"),
        kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Size: kit.Sm, OnClick: func() { saved++ }, Children: h.Text("Save")})
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Save"))
fmt.Println("saved", saved)
// Output: saved 1
```

### type Calendar

```go
type Calendar struct {
    // Value points to the selected date of a controlled calendar; nil
    // leaves it to the calendar, which starts at DefaultValue.
    Value        *aria.Date
    DefaultValue aria.Date
    // OnValueChange is called with the date the user selects.
    OnValueChange func(aria.Date)

    // Min and Max bound the dates that can be focused or selected, both
    // included; the zero Date is no limit. Dates outside them are dimmed
    // and the month buttons stop at them.
    Min, Max aria.Date
    // IsDateUnavailable marks dates that are shown dimmed and can not be
    // selected (booked days, holidays).
    IsDateUnavailable func(aria.Date) bool
    // Disabled disables every date; ReadOnly keeps them focusable but not
    // selectable.
    Disabled, ReadOnly bool
    // FocusedDate points to the focused date of a controlled calendar, the
    // one with the tab stop, whose month is on display; nil leaves it to the
    // calendar, which starts at DefaultFocusedDate, else the selected date,
    // else today. OnFocusChange is called when it changes.
    FocusedDate        *aria.Date
    DefaultFocusedDate aria.Date
    OnFocusChange      func(aria.Date)
    // VisibleMonths is the number of months shown side by side (1 to 12,
    // default 1; the layout is a column below the md breakpoint).
    VisibleMonths int
    // FirstDayOfWeek is the first column; nil takes the locale's.
    FirstDayOfWeek *time.Weekday
    // FixedWeeks always shows six weeks per month, so the calendar keeps
    // its height from month to month.
    FixedWeeks bool
    // HideOutsideDays leaves out the dates of the neighbouring months that
    // fill the first and last week (shadcn shows them by default).
    HideOutsideDays bool
    // NarrowWeekdays writes the column headers with the narrowest weekday
    // names (one letter, usually) instead of the short ones ("M" for "Mo"):
    // for a locale whose short names do not fit a 32 px cell, such as
    // Arabic's. The headers keep the full weekday as their name for
    // assistive technologies.
    NarrowWeekdays bool
    // Today is the date drawn as today; the zero Date is the current day.
    // Set it to make a test or a golden deterministic.
    Today aria.Date
    // Locale is the BCP 47 tag of the names, digits, first weekday and
    // direction; empty is the component's locale (i18n.UseLocale).
    // Direction is "ltr" or "rtl"; empty follows the Locale when one is
    // given, else the direction at the calendar's position
    // (tela.UseDirection: the nearest h.Dir above it). Either one given
    // here also sets the direction of the calendar's layout.
    Locale, Direction string
    // AriaLabel names the calendar ("Appointment date"); the visible month
    // is appended. PreviousLabel and NextLabel name the month buttons
    // ("Previous" and "Next" by default: translate them with i18n.T).
    AriaLabel                string
    PreviousLabel, NextLabel string
    // PreviousIcon and NextIcon replace the chevrons of the month buttons.
    PreviousIcon, NextIcon tela.Icon

    // Class is added after the recipe's Root classes; the other Class fields
    // do the same for their part: the months row, a month, the nav row, a
    // caption, a weekday name, a day cell and a day button.
    Class          string
    MonthsClass    string
    MonthClass     string
    NavClass       string
    CaptionClass   string
    WeekdayClass   string
    DayClass       string
    DayButtonClass string
    // Props are more props for the root element.
    Props tela.Child
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Calendar is a month grid that selects one date, shadcn/ui's Calendar (react-day-picker's look) on aria.UseCalendar: a caption with the month and year between the previous and next buttons, the weekday names, and a ghost button for each day, with today, the selected date, the dates of the neighbouring months and the dates that can not be selected each styled.

```go
day, setDay := tela.UseState(aria.Date{})
kit.Calendar{Value: &day, OnValueChange: setDay.Set, Min: aria.Today()}
```

It is one tab stop: Tab reaches the focused date and the arrow keys move over the days (a week with up and down, swapped by a right-to-left direction), PageUp and PageDown over the months (a year with Shift), Home and End to the first and last day of the week, and Enter or Space select. The month on display follows the focus. Names, digits, the first day of the week and the direction come from package i18n: the component's locale, or Locale.

The selected date follows the kit's value rule with the Date type of package aria, a comparable day with no zone: Value (a pointer to your state) with OnValueChange controls it, DefaultValue starts an uncontrolled one; the zero Date is none. See [`RangeCalendar`](#type-rangecalendar) for a range and [`DatePicker`](#type-datepicker) for a calendar in a popover.

Deviations from shadcn: react-day-picker's year and month dropdowns (captionLayout), week numbers and its other modes (several dates) are not ported; outside dates that belong to another visible month are hidden, as there; the date cell's aria-label is the full localized date without "Today" or "selected" (aria-selected carries the state).

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
var picked aria.Date
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"), kit.Calendar{
        // Today is injected so the example does not depend on the clock;
        // leave it out in an app.
        Today:         aria.Date{Year: 2026, Month: time.October, Day: 25},
        Min:           aria.Date{Year: 2026, Month: time.October, Day: 8},
        OnValueChange: func(day aria.Date) { picked = day },
    })
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page, telatest.Size(400, 400))
// Tab skips the previous button (disabled at Min) and reaches today's
// date; PageDown moves a month and Enter chooses.
app.Press("Tab")
app.Press("Tab")
app.Press("PageDown")
app.Press("Enter")
fmt.Println(picked)
// Output: 2026-11-25
```


### type CalendarStyle

```go
type CalendarStyle struct {
    // Root is the calendar: padding, background, the width of its content.
    Root string
    // Months holds the nav and the months, side by side from md up.
    Months string
    // Month is one month: its caption and its grid.
    Month string
    // Nav is the row of the previous and next buttons, over the captions.
    Nav string
    // ButtonPrevious and ButtonNext are added to the ghost button's classes
    // (the Button recipe's Root, Ghost variant and default size).
    ButtonPrevious, ButtonNext string
    // Chevron is the arrow icon of the nav buttons; rtl:rotate-180 turns it
    // around under a right-to-left direction.
    Chevron string
    // MonthCaption holds the month's title and CaptionLabel is the title.
    MonthCaption, CaptionLabel string
    // MonthGrid is the grid element of a month, Weekdays the row of weekday
    // names, Weekday one name, and Week one row of days.
    MonthGrid, Weekdays, Weekday, Week string
    // Day is the cell of a date: it sizes the day and carries the
    // background of today and of the ends of a range behind the button.
    Day string
    // Today, Outside, Disabled, Hidden, RangeStart, RangeMiddle and
    // RangeEnd are added to Day for a date in that state (react-day-picker's
    // modifiers). Disabled is a date that can not be selected (before Min,
    // after Max, unavailable); Hidden an outside date that is not shown.
    Today, Outside, Disabled, Hidden, RangeStart, RangeMiddle, RangeEnd string
    // TodayWithSelected is added to Day when today is selected
    // (shadcn's data-[selected=true]:rounded-none on the today modifier).
    TodayWithSelected string
    // DayButton is the button of a date, a ghost icon button resized to
    // fill its cell.
    DayButton string
    // DayButtonWithSelected is added to DayButton for the selected date of
    // a Calendar (shadcn's data-[selected-single=true]:), and
    // DayButtonWithRangeStart, DayButtonWithRangeMiddle and
    // DayButtonWithRangeEnd for the parts of a selected range.
    DayButtonWithSelected, DayButtonWithRangeStart, DayButtonWithRangeMiddle, DayButtonWithRangeEnd string
}
```

CalendarStyle is the recipe of [`Calendar`](#type-calendar) and [`RangeCalendar`](#type-rangecalendar) (shadcn/ui's Calendar, whose parts are react-day-picker's: its classNames). The root element is the calendar; a day is a cell (Day) that holds a ghost icon button (DayButton), as in react-day-picker's td and button.

shadcn sizes the calendar with the CSS variable --cell-size (2rem); the engine has no variables, so the recipe writes size-8, h-8, px-8 and min-w-8 where shadcn writes size-(--cell-size) and the like: change them together to resize the cells.

### type Card

```go
type Card struct {
    // Title and Description are the header's heading and its muted line.
    Title, Description tela.Component
    // TitleLevel makes the Title a heading of that level, 1 to 6 (h1 to
    // h6); 0 keeps shadcn's div. A level outside 0 to 6 panics in dev mode
    // and is clamped otherwise.
    TitleLevel int
    // Action sits at the header's right end: a button, a menu.
    Action tela.Component
    // Children is the content.
    Children tela.Component
    // Footer is the card's last row.
    Footer tela.Component

    // Class is added after the recipe's Root classes. The other Class
    // fields do the same for their part.
    Class            string
    HeaderClass      string
    TitleClass       string
    DescriptionClass string
    ActionClass      string
    ContentClass     string
    FooterClass      string
    // Props are more props for the root element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

Card is a surface with a header, content and a footer, shadcn/ui's Card. Its parts are slots; an absent slot (nil) draws nothing, and the header is drawn when the card has a Title, a Description or an Action.

```go
kit.Card{
    Title:       h.Text("Create project"),
    Description: h.Text("Deploy your new project in one click."),
    Action:      kit.Button{Variant: kit.Ghost, Size: kit.IconSm, Icon: icons.X, AriaLabel: "Close"},
    Children:    form,
    Footer:      h.Fragment(kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Children: h.Text("Cancel")}, ...),
}
```

The Title is a div, as in shadcn. TitleLevel from 1 to 6 makes it a heading (h1 to h6) with the same classes, so that assistive technologies list it and a screen reader user can jump to it; give it the level that fits the page's outline, with plain text in Title:

```go
kit.Card{TitleLevel: 2, Title: h.Text("Notifications")}
```

The recipe's Header, Title, Description, Action, Content and Footer classes style the parts; the fields ending in Class add to them for one card.

shadcn's \[.border-b\]:pb-6 and \[.border-t\]:pt-6 (a header or footer that has a border brings its own padding) are not in the recipe: add pb-6 or pt-6 with HeaderClass and FooterClass when you add the border.

### type Checkbox

```go
type Checkbox struct {
    // Checked points to the state of a controlled checkbox; nil leaves it
    // to the checkbox, which starts at DefaultChecked.
    Checked *bool
    // DefaultChecked is the initial state of an uncontrolled checkbox.
    DefaultChecked bool
    // OnCheckedChange is called with the next state when the user toggles
    // the checkbox. For a controlled checkbox it is how the change is asked
    // for.
    OnCheckedChange func(bool)
    // Disabled makes the checkbox inert and dims it.
    Disabled bool
    // Required marks the checkbox as one the user must check
    // (aria-required).
    Required bool
    // Invalid marks the value as wrong: assistive technologies announce it
    // and the aria-invalid: classes (a red border and ring) apply. A
    // [Field] with an Error sets it on its control.
    Invalid bool
    // ID is the checkbox's id, for a [Label]'s For. Inside a [Field] it
    // defaults to the field's.
    ID string
    // AriaLabel names a checkbox that has no label of its own.
    AriaLabel string
    // Icon replaces the check mark (Lucide's check).
    Icon tela.Icon
    // Class is added after the recipe's classes; IndicatorClass and
    // IconClass do the same for their parts.
    Class          string
    IndicatorClass string
    IconClass      string
    // Props are more props for the checkbox element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

Checkbox is a box that is checked or not, shadcn/ui's Checkbox, on aria.UseCheckbox: a click or Space toggles it, Tab reaches it, and it has the checkbox role and aria-checked. Its state follows the kit's rule: give Checked (a pointer to your state) and OnCheckedChange to keep it yourself, or DefaultChecked to let the checkbox keep it.

```go
agree, setAgree := tela.UseState(false)
kit.Checkbox{Checked: &agree, OnCheckedChange: setAgree.Set, AriaLabel: "Accept the terms"}
```

A [`Label`](#type-label) with the checkbox's ID names it and toggles it when clicked, and a [`Field`](#type-field) ties its label to it with no ids to write:

```go
kit.Field{Orientation: kit.Horizontal, Label: "Accept the terms",
    Children: kit.Checkbox{DefaultChecked: true}}
```

The indeterminate state is not supported (aria has none yet).

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
agreed := false
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("flex items-center gap-3"),
        kit.Checkbox{ID: "terms", OnCheckedChange: func(b bool) { agreed = b }},
        kit.Label{For: "terms", Children: h.Text("Accept the terms")})
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByText("Accept the terms")) // the label toggles the checkbox
fmt.Println("agreed", agreed)
// Output: agreed true
```


```go
    // Root is the box: size, border, the checked colors, focus ring,
    // disabled and invalid. It has the class "peer", so a sibling after it
    // can use the peer-* variants. It is inline-flex with its content centered,
    // as a browser draws the content of a button (Tela's button centers it
    // horizontally only).
    Root string
    // Indicator holds the check mark and is only there while checked.
    Indicator string
    // Icon is the check mark.
    Icon string
}
```

CheckboxStyle is the recipe of [`Checkbox`](#type-checkbox) (shadcn/ui's Checkbox).

### type ColorInput

```go
type ColorInput struct {
    // The color, as in [ColorPicker].
    Value         *tela.Color
    DefaultValue  *tela.Color
    OnValueChange func(tela.Color)
    OnValueCommit func(tela.Color)
    Alpha         bool
    Swatches      []tela.Color
    // Disabled makes the button inert and dims it, and the panel never opens.
    Disabled bool
    // Trigger is the element that opens the panel; nil is an outline
    // [Button] with the swatch and the code.
    Trigger Trigger
    // Placement, Align and Offset place the panel as a [Popover]'s do: below
    // the button, at its start, by default.
    Placement, Align string
    Offset           float32

    // Open points to the open state of a controlled panel, as a
    // [Popover]'s does.
    Open         *bool
    DefaultOpen  bool
    OnOpenChange func(open bool)

    // AreaLabel, HueLabel, AlphaLabel and HexLabel name the picker's
    // controls, as in [ColorPicker].
    AreaLabel, HueLabel, AlphaLabel, HexLabel string
    // AriaLabel names the button, followed by its color ("Brand color,
    // #6366f1"), and the panel ("Color picker" when it is empty); inside a
    // [Field] with a Label that label is used. The color in the name is the
    // one of the last build, while the code shown on the button follows a
    // drag: an uncontrolled drag names the color it ends on when it ends
    // (or when the pointer rests), as the picker's thumbs do with their
    // aria-valuetext, so assistive technology is not told every move; a
    // controlled ColorInput builds on every change. ID is the button's id,
    // for a [Label]'s For, and inside a Field defaults to the field's. With
    // a Trigger of your own, these are for the panel only: name the button
    // and give it its id yourself.
    AriaLabel string
    ID        string
    // Direction is "ltr" or "rtl"; empty is the direction at the component's
    // position (tela.UseDirection: the nearest h.Dir above it, left to right
    // without one). Under "rtl" the saturation grows toward the left
    // of the area, the hue and the opacity toward the left of their sliders,
    // and ArrowLeft increases them; a Direction given here also sets the
    // direction of the panel's layout, not the button's.
    Direction string

    // Class is added to the default button's classes; PanelClass to the
    // picker's root; PopoverClass to the popover's panel.
    Class        string
    PanelClass   string
    PopoverClass string
    // Props are more props for the default button.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

ColorInput is a button that shows a color and opens a [`ColorPicker`](#type-colorpicker) in a [`Popover`](#type-popover) to change it: the swatch and the hex code on a button, the picker in a panel under it. It takes the values of a ColorPicker and the open state of a Popover.

```go
kit.ColorInput{DefaultValue: new(tela.Hex("#6366f1")), Alpha: true, OnValueCommit: save}
```

The color lives in the ColorInput, not in the panel, so the swatch and the code on the button follow a drag in the panel without building the component on every move, and the color survives the panel being closed. The panel is a dialog; the focus goes into it when it opens and returns to the button when it closes (Escape, or a press outside it).

Trigger replaces the button, with the rule of every trigger slot (see [`Trigger`](#type-trigger)): the button is the one you write, with the popover's props. Then nothing on it shows the color unless you draw it from OnValueChange.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"), kit.ColorInput{DefaultValue: new(tela.Hex("#6366f1")), Swatches: []tela.Color{tela.Hex("#ef4444"), tela.Hex("#22c55e")}})
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "#6366f1"))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "#22c55e"))
app.Press("Escape")
app.Expect(telatest.ByRole("button", "#22c55e"), telatest.Expanded(false))
// Output:
```

### type ColorInputStyle

```go
type ColorInputStyle struct {
    // Trigger is added to the classes of the outline [Button] that is the
    // default trigger.
    Trigger string
    // Swatch is the small square of the color inside the trigger.
    Swatch string
    // Code is the hex code inside the trigger. Inter is proportional, so
    // its digits are tabular (tabular-nums) and its minimum width is that
    // of the widest code, "#" and six digits (the digits are wider than the
    // letters a to f, which the code is written with), so the button does
    // not change size while the color does. CodeAlpha is added to Code
    // while the input has Alpha, with the width of "#" and eight digits.
    // The widths are in em, for Inter at any size; another font needs its
    // own.
    Code      string
    CodeAlpha string
}
```

ColorInputStyle is the recipe of [`ColorInput`](#type-colorinput).

### type ColorPicker

```go
type ColorPicker struct {
    // Value points to the color of a controlled picker; nil leaves it to
    // the picker, which starts at DefaultValue. OnValueChange is called with
    // the next color on every change.
    Value *tela.Color
    // DefaultValue is the color of an uncontrolled picker at the start; nil
    // starts at opaque black (tela.Black). It is a pointer because the zero
    // Color is a color too, transparent black.
    DefaultValue  *tela.Color
    OnValueChange func(tela.Color)
    // OnValueCommit is called with the color when the user stops changing
    // it, and not for a change that left it as it was.
    OnValueCommit func(tela.Color)
    // Alpha adds the opacity slider and lets the hex field take and show
    // the opacity (#rrggbbaa). Without it the field shows #rrggbb and the
    // color keeps whatever opacity it had.
    Alpha bool
    // Swatches are preset colors: buttons that set the color.
    Swatches []tela.Color
    // Disabled dims the picker and makes it ignore the user.
    Disabled bool
    // AreaLabel, HueLabel, AlphaLabel and HexLabel name the controls for
    // assistive technologies ("Color area", "Hue", "Alpha" and "Hex" by
    // default); set them for another language. The value texts ("Hue
    // 180°") are aria's English ones.
    AreaLabel, HueLabel, AlphaLabel, HexLabel string
    // Direction is "ltr" or "rtl"; empty is the direction at the component's
    // position (tela.UseDirection: the nearest h.Dir above it, left to right
    // without one). Under "rtl" the saturation grows toward the left
    // of the area, the hue and the opacity toward the left of their sliders,
    // and ArrowLeft increases them; a Direction given here also sets the
    // direction of the panel's layout.
    Direction string
    // ID is the id of the picker's hex field, for a [Label]'s For. Inside
    // a [Field] it defaults to the field's, so the field's label points to
    // it and a press on the label focuses it.
    ID string
    // AriaLabel names the picker as a group for assistive technologies;
    // inside a Field with a Label that label is used. A picker with neither
    // is not a group.
    AriaLabel string
    // Class is added after the recipe's Root classes. Props are more props
    // for the root element.
    Class string
    Props tela.Child
}
```

ColorPicker lets people choose a color: an area for saturation and brightness, a slider for the hue, optionally one for the opacity, a field for the hex code, and optionally a row of preset colors. The value is a [`tela.Color`](API-Reference-tela#type-color), and the picker follows the kit's rule for values.

```go
c, setC := tela.UseState(tela.Hex("#6366f1"))
kit.ColorPicker{Value: &c, OnValueChange: setC.Set, Alpha: true,
    Swatches: []tela.Color{tela.Hex("#ef4444"), tela.Hex("#22c55e"), tela.Hex("#3b82f6")}}
```

It is built on the color hooks of package aria (aria.UseColorState, the area, the sliders and the field), so the area and the sliders are dragged with a mouse, a finger or a pen, the arrow keys move a thumb by one step (Shift or Page Up and Page Down by more) and each control is announced with its value. The hue is kept when the color goes through a gray or black, so dragging to the left edge of the area does not lose it.

Dragging only repaints: the thumbs, the area, the preview, the hex field (unless it is being typed in) and the alpha track follow the pointer without the picker being built on every move. OnValueChange is called on every change, so a controlled picker builds as often as the state it is given does; OnValueCommit is called once when the user stops (a drag ends, a key, a swatch or a hex code changed the color), which is the moment to save it.

The hex field accepts "#rgb", "#rrggbb" (and with Alpha the forms with four or eight digits) with or without the "#", commits on Enter and when it loses the focus, and goes back to the color when the text is not a code. Use [`ColorInput`](#type-colorinput) for a picker that opens from a button.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
var saved []string
page := func() tela.Node {
    c, setC := tela.UseState(tela.Hex("#6366f1"))
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-4"),
        kit.ColorPicker{Value: &c, OnValueChange: setC.Set, Alpha: true,
            Swatches:      []tela.Color{tela.Hex("#ef4444"), tela.Hex("#22c55e")},
            OnValueCommit: func(c tela.Color) { saved = append(saved, aria.FormatHexColor(c, true)) }},
        h.P(h.Textf("Chosen: %s", aria.FormatHexColor(c, false))))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "#22c55e"))
app.Focus(telatest.ByRole("slider", "Alpha"))
app.Press("PageDown")
app.ExpectText("Chosen: #22c55e")
fmt.Println(strings.Join(saved, " "))
// Output: #22c55eff #22c55ee5
```

#### func (ColorPicker) Build

```go
func (p ColorPicker) Build() tela.Node
```

Build returns the picker. Inside a [`Field`](#type-field) the hex field takes the field's id, description and invalid state, and the picker is named by the field's label.

### type ColorPickerStyle

```go
type ColorPickerStyle struct {
    // Root is the panel: a column that is 16rem wide, which is the room
    // inside a [Popover]'s p-4 and w-72.
    Root string
    // Disabled is added to the root while the picker is disabled.
    Disabled string
    // Area is the saturation and brightness area. Its background is the
    // hue at full saturation and brightness, which the component paints
    // live; AreaSaturation and AreaBrightness are the white and black
    // gradients over it.
    Area           string
    AreaSaturation string
    AreaBrightness string
    // AreaThumb is the round handle on the area.
    AreaThumb string
    // Slider is the row of a hue or alpha slider: the track, and the thumb
    // on top of it.
    Slider string
    // Track is the groove of a slider; HueTrack adds the rainbow to it and
    // AlphaTrack adds the checkerboard (the color's gradient is drawn over
    // it by AlphaFill).
    Track      string
    HueTrack   string
    AlphaTrack string
    AlphaFill  string
    // Thumb is the round handle of a slider. It is centered on the point
    // the value stands for, so it hangs over the ends of the track.
    Thumb string
    // Checkerboard is the pattern under everything that can be
    // transparent: the alpha track, the preview and the swatches. It is a
    // conic gradient that repeats every 12px (two squares of 6px).
    Checkerboard string
    // Row is the line of the preview and the hex field.
    Row string
    // Preview is the swatch next to the hex field; it holds the color.
    Preview string
    // Input is added to the classes of the kit's [Input] on the hex field.
    Input string
    // Swatches is the wrapping row of preset colors; Swatch is one of
    // them and SwatchSelected is added to the one that is the color now.
    Swatches       string
    Swatch         string
    SwatchSelected string
}
```

ColorPickerStyle is the recipe of [`ColorPicker`](#type-colorpicker) and of the panel [`ColorInput`](#type-colorinput) opens. shadcn/ui has no color picker: the look is the kit's own, written in shadcn's language (ADR-143).

### type Column

```go
type Column[T any] struct {
    // ID names the column in a [SortState]; it defaults to Header and must
    // be unique in the table.
    ID string
    // Header is the column's title, and the name of its sort button.
    Header string
    // HeaderContent is drawn in place of the Header text, for a header that
    // is not plain text. Header still names the column.
    HeaderContent tela.Component
    // Cell returns the content of the column's cell for a row, such as
    // h.Text(u.Name). It is a flex item of the cell: return one node.
    Cell func(row T) tela.Node
    // Sort orders two rows by this column (negative when a comes first, as
    // strings.Compare and cmp.Compare). A column with a Sort is sortable:
    // its header is a button that cycles the order.
    Sort func(a, b T) int
    // Sortable makes a column without a Sort sortable, for rows that come
    // sorted (from a server): the table shows the sort state and reports a
    // change with OnSortChange, and leaves the rows in the order given.
    Sortable bool
    // Width is the column's grid track: "200px", "1fr", "auto", "minmax(120px, 1fr)",
    // "min-content"... The default is "auto".
    Width string
    // Align is AlignLeft (the default), AlignCenter or AlignRight; the first
    // and the last are the start and the end of the line (see ColumnAlign).
    Align ColumnAlign
    // Sticky keeps the column in place when the table scrolls
    // horizontally. Sticky columns come first, and every sticky column
    // but the last has a Width in px ("160px"), since the next one sticks
    // right after it.
    Sticky bool
    // Footer is the column's cell of the footer row; the row is drawn when
    // any column has one. FooterSpan, 2 or more, makes it span that many
    // columns (shadcn's colSpan), and the columns it covers have no
    // footer cell of their own.
    Footer     tela.Component
    FooterSpan int
    // Class is added to the column's body cells, HeaderClass to its header
    // and FooterClass to its footer cell.
    Class, HeaderClass, FooterClass string
    // CellProps returns more props for the column's cell of a row, such as
    // h.TestID or a handler; HeaderProps and FooterProps are the props of
    // the header and footer cells.
    CellProps                func(row T) tela.Child
    HeaderProps, FooterProps tela.Child
}
```

Column describes a column of a [`Table`](#type-table) of rows of type T.

### type ColumnAlign

```go
type ColumnAlign string
```

ColumnAlign is the horizontal alignment of a [`Column`](#type-column)'s header, cells and footer. The zero value is left, as shadcn's `text-left`. Left and right are the start and the end of the line: under a right-to-left direction (h.Dir("rtl")) the table mirrors and AlignRight is at the left, where numbers belong, as in shadcn's right-to-left registry (text-start and text-end).

```go
const (
    AlignLeft   ColumnAlign = ""
    AlignCenter ColumnAlign = "center"
    AlignRight  ColumnAlign = "right"
)
```

### type ContextMenu

```go
type ContextMenu[K comparable] struct {
    // Children is the area: what a right click opens the menu on.
    Children tela.Component
    // Items are the entries of the menu, in order.
    Items []MenuItem[K]
    // OnSelect is called with the key of a plain item when it is chosen,
    // after the item's own OnSelect.
    OnSelect func(K)
    // Disabled leaves the area's right click to the platform and to an
    // outer context menu.
    Disabled bool
    // NoLongPress keeps a touch or a pen that stays down from opening the
    // menu, so that it clicks what it is on (a held mouse button always
    // does: see aria.ContextMenuTriggerOptions).
    NoLongPress bool
    // AriaLabel names the menu, which has no name of its own: the area is
    // not a label.
    AriaLabel string
    // CheckIcon and RadioIcon replace the check of a checkbox item and the
    // dot of a radio item.
    CheckIcon, RadioIcon tela.Icon

    // Open points to the open state of a controlled menu; nil leaves it to
    // the component. OnOpenChange is called with the next state.
    Open         *bool
    OnOpenChange func(open bool)

    // Class is added to the area (it has no classes of its own);
    // ContentClass is added after the recipe's Content classes, to the
    // menu's panel.
    Class        string
    ContentClass string
    // Props are more props for the area element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

ContextMenu is a menu that opens where the user right-clicks inside an area, shadcn/ui's ContextMenu, built on aria.UseContextMenuTrigger: a right click opens it at the pointer, a touch or a pen that stays down opens it under the finger, and Shift+F10 or the ContextMenu key opens it, on its first item, at the area's top-left corner. The keys reach the area from the element that has the focus inside it, as in the browser: an area with nothing focusable inside opens from the keyboard only when it can take the focus itself (Props: h.TabIndex(0), with a focus-visible: ring in Class). The menu closes with Escape, a press outside it with any mouse button or choosing an item, and the focus returns to where it was. A right click elsewhere in the area while the menu is open closes it and opens a new one at the new point (Radix), a right click in another area opens that area's menu instead, and in nested areas the innermost wins.

```go
kit.ContextMenu[string]{
    AriaLabel: "Actions",
    Class:     "flex h-40 w-72 items-center justify-center rounded-md border border-dashed text-sm",
    Children:  h.Text("Right click here"),
    Items: []kit.MenuItem[string]{
        {Key: "back", Label: "Back", Shortcut: "⌘["},
        {Key: "reload", Label: "Reload", Shortcut: "⌘R"},
        {Kind: kit.MenuSeparator},
        {Kind: kit.MenuCheckbox, Key: "bookmarks", Label: "Show bookmarks", DefaultChecked: true},
    },
}
```

The items are the \[MenuItem\]s of [`DropdownMenu`](#type-dropdownmenu), with no submenus yet (ADR-141). The root element is the area, a div that holds Children; the area is not focusable by itself, the keys reach it from what inside it has the focus, and a keyboard menu opens at the area's corner, not at that element (ADR-133). Open and OnOpenChange are the usual controlled pair (a menu opens at a point, so there is no DefaultOpen).

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"), kit.ContextMenu[string]{
        AriaLabel: "Actions",
        Class:     "flex h-40 w-72 items-center justify-center rounded-md border border-dashed text-sm",
        Children:  h.Button(h.Text("Right click here")),
        Items: []kit.MenuItem[string]{
            {Key: "back", Label: "Back", Shortcut: "⌘["},
            {Key: "reload", Label: "Reload", Shortcut: "⌘R"},
        },
        OnSelect: func(key string) { fmt.Println("chose", key) },
    })
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
// Shift+F10 opens the menu from the keyboard; a right click opens it at
// the pointer.
app.Focus(telatest.ByRole("button", "Right click here"))
app.Press("Shift+F10")
app.Press("ArrowDown")
app.Press("Enter")
// Output: chose reload
```

#### func (ContextMenu[K]) Build

```go
func (c ContextMenu[K]) Build() tela.Node
```

Build returns the area and, in a portal, the menu.

### type DatePicker

```go
type DatePicker struct {
    // Value points to the chosen date of a controlled picker; nil leaves it
    // to the picker, which starts at DefaultValue. OnValueChange is called
    // with the date the user chooses.
    Value         *aria.Date
    DefaultValue  aria.Date
    OnValueChange func(aria.Date)
    // Placeholder is shown while no date is chosen; the default is "Pick a
    // date".
    Placeholder string
    // Format writes the chosen date on the button; nil is the formatter's
    // long date ("October 25, 2026").
    Format func(f i18n.Formatter, d aria.Date) string

    // Min, Max, IsDateUnavailable, VisibleMonths, FirstDayOfWeek,
    // FixedWeeks, HideOutsideDays, NarrowWeekdays, Today, Locale, Direction,
    // PreviousLabel and NextLabel are those of [Calendar].
    Min, Max                 aria.Date
    IsDateUnavailable        func(aria.Date) bool
    VisibleMonths            int
    FirstDayOfWeek           *time.Weekday
    FixedWeeks               bool
    HideOutsideDays          bool
    NarrowWeekdays           bool
    Today                    aria.Date
    Locale, Direction        string
    PreviousLabel, NextLabel string

    // Disabled makes the picker inert and dims it.
    Disabled bool
    // Invalid marks the picker as wrong: assistive technologies announce it
    // and the button's aria-invalid: classes (a red border and ring) apply.
    // A [Field] with an Error sets it.
    Invalid bool
    // ID is the button's id, for a [Label]'s For. Inside a [Field] it
    // defaults to the field's.
    ID string
    // AriaLabel names the picker, and the popover; inside a Field with a
    // Label that label is used. The chosen date is appended to the button's
    // name.
    AriaLabel string
    // Icon replaces the calendar icon of the button.
    Icon tela.Icon
    // Align is where the popover sits along the button: "start" (the
    // default), "center" or "end".
    Align string
    // KeepOpen leaves the popover open after a date is chosen.
    KeepOpen bool
    // Open points to the open state of a controlled popover; nil leaves it
    // to the picker, which starts at DefaultOpen. OnOpenChange is called with
    // the next state.
    Open         *bool
    DefaultOpen  bool
    OnOpenChange func(open bool)

    // Class is added after the recipe's Root classes, to the button; the
    // other Class fields do the same for the popover's panel and the
    // calendar.
    Class         string
    PopoverClass  string
    CalendarClass string
    // Props are more props for the button element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

DatePicker is a button that shows a date and opens a calendar to choose it, shadcn/ui's date picker pattern: an outline [`Button`](#type-button) with a calendar icon and the date, or a placeholder, that toggles a [`Popover`](#type-popover) holding a [`Calendar`](#type-calendar). Choosing a date closes the popover and puts the focus back on the button; Escape and a press outside close it without choosing.

```go
day, setDay := tela.UseState(aria.Date{})
kit.DatePicker{Value: &day, OnValueChange: setDay.Set, Min: aria.Today()}
```

The date follows the kit's value rule with the aria.Date type (the zero Date is none): Value (a pointer to your state) with OnValueChange controls it, DefaultValue starts an uncontrolled picker. The button shows the date as the component's locale writes it in its long form ("October 25, 2026"); Format changes that. The focus moves into the calendar, onto the date, when the popover opens, and the calendar follows the picker's locale for its names, digits, first weekday and direction (Locale).

Inside a [`Field`](#type-field) the button takes the field's id, so the label points to it and names it, the field's description or error describes it, and an error marks it invalid.

Limits (Min, Max), IsDateUnavailable, FirstDayOfWeek, FixedWeeks, HideOutsideDays and Today are those of [`Calendar`](#type-calendar); for several months or a range see [`DateRangePicker`](#type-daterangepicker). There is no time of day and no typed date: the date is chosen in the calendar.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"), kit.DatePicker{
        AriaLabel: "Birthday",
        Today:     aria.Date{Year: 2026, Month: time.October, Day: 25},
        OnValueChange: func(day aria.Date) {
            fmt.Println("chose", day)
        },
    })
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page, telatest.Size(400, 480))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Birthday"))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("gridcell", "Friday, October 9, 2026"))
// The popover closed and the button shows the date.
app.ExpectText("October 9, 2026")
fmt.Println("open:", app.Count(telatest.ByRole("application", "")) == 1)
// Output:
// chose 2026-10-09
// open: false
```


Build returns the button and its popover.

### type DateRangePicker

```go
type DateRangePicker struct {
    // Value points to the chosen range of a controlled picker; nil leaves it
    // to the picker, which starts at DefaultValue. OnValueChange is called
    // with the range the user completes.
    Value         *aria.DateRange
    DefaultValue  aria.DateRange
    OnValueChange func(aria.DateRange)
    // Placeholder is shown while no range is chosen; the default is "Pick a
    // date range".
    Placeholder string
    // Format writes the chosen range on the button; nil writes both ends in
    // the formatter's medium form joined by " - ".
    Format func(f i18n.Formatter, r aria.DateRange) string
    // AllowsNonContiguousRanges lets a range cross unavailable dates.
    AllowsNonContiguousRanges bool

    Min, Max                 aria.Date
    IsDateUnavailable        func(aria.Date) bool
    VisibleMonths            int
    FirstDayOfWeek           *time.Weekday
    FixedWeeks               bool
    HideOutsideDays          bool
    NarrowWeekdays           bool
    Today                    aria.Date
    Locale, Direction        string
    PreviousLabel, NextLabel string

    Disabled      bool
    Invalid       bool
    ID            string
    AriaLabel     string
    Icon          tela.Icon
    Align         string
    KeepOpen      bool
    Open          *bool
    DefaultOpen   bool
    OnOpenChange  func(open bool)
    Class         string
    PopoverClass  string
    CalendarClass string
    Props         tela.Child
}
```

DateRangePicker is a [`DatePicker`](#type-datepicker) for a span of dates, shadcn/ui's date range picker: the button shows the two ends ("Oct 20, 2026 - Nov 5, 2026") and the popover holds a [`RangeCalendar`](#type-rangecalendar) of two months. The popover closes when the second date completes the range (or stays open with KeepOpen); the first Escape in the calendar cancels an anchored range, and the next closes the popover.

```go
var stay aria.DateRange
kit.DateRangePicker{OnValueChange: func(r aria.DateRange) { stay = r }}
```

The value follows the kit's rule with aria.DateRange. VisibleMonths defaults to 2 here, as in shadcn's demo; the other fields are those of [`DatePicker`](#type-datepicker) and [`RangeCalendar`](#type-rangecalendar).

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"), kit.DateRangePicker{
        AriaLabel: "Stay",
        Today:     aria.Date{Year: 2026, Month: time.October, Day: 25},
        OnValueChange: func(r aria.DateRange) {
            fmt.Println("stay", r.Start, r.End)
        },
    })
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page, telatest.Size(800, 480))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Stay"))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("gridcell", "Tuesday, October 27, 2026"))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("gridcell", "Saturday, October 31, 2026"))
// Output: stay 2026-10-27 2026-10-31
```

### type Dialog

```go
type Dialog struct {
    // Trigger is the element that opens the dialog; nil for a dialog
    // opened only by its state.
    Trigger Trigger
    // Title and Description name and describe the dialog for assistive
    // technologies and sit in its header. Give a dialog that has no visible
    // title an AriaLabel.
    Title, Description tela.Component
    // Children is the content, between the header and the footer.
    Children tela.Component
    // Footer is the row of actions at the bottom, usually buttons.
    Footer tela.Component
    // HideClose leaves out the close button in the top-right corner, which
    // is drawn by default (shadcn's showCloseButton={false}). CloseIcon and
    // CloseLabel are for the button when it is drawn.
    HideClose bool
    // CloseIcon replaces the X of the close button; CloseLabel is its
    // accessible name ("Close").
    CloseIcon  tela.Icon
    CloseLabel string
    // AriaLabel names a dialog that has no Title.
    AriaLabel string

    // Open points to the open state of a controlled dialog; nil leaves the
    // state to the dialog, which starts closed unless DefaultOpen is set.
    // OnOpenChange is called with the next state when the trigger, Escape,
    // a press on the scrim or the close button asks for a change.
    Open         *bool
    DefaultOpen  bool
    OnOpenChange func(open bool)
    // Disabled disables the trigger, which is then inert and dimmed by its
    // recipe; the dialog does not open. Set it here: the trigger props
    // override a Disabled given to the trigger component itself.
    Disabled bool

    // Class is added after the recipe's Root classes, to the panel. The
    // other Class fields do the same for their part.
    Class            string
    OverlayClass     string
    HeaderClass      string
    TitleClass       string
    DescriptionClass string
    FooterClass      string
    CloseClass       string
    // Props are more props for the dialog element (the panel).
    Props tela.Child
}
```

Dialog is a modal window over the page, shadcn/ui's Dialog: a trigger, and a panel with a title, a description, content and a footer that opens in the middle of the window over a scrim. While it is open the page is inert, Tab stays inside the dialog, Escape and a press on the scrim close it, and the focus goes back to the trigger. It fades and scales in and out.

```go
kit.Dialog{
    Trigger:     kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Children: h.Text("Edit profile")},
    Title:       h.Text("Edit profile"),
    Description: h.Text("Make changes to your profile here."),
    Children:    form,
    Footer:      kit.Button{Children: h.Text("Save changes")},
}
```

The Trigger slot is a [`Trigger`](#type-trigger): a [`Button`](#type-button), or anything made one with [`TriggerFunc`](#type-triggerfunc). Without a Trigger the dialog is opened from your state:

```go
kit.Dialog{Open: &open, OnOpenChange: setOpen.Set, Title: h.Text("Welcome")}
```

The panel exists only while the dialog is open, so the state of what is inside it starts afresh each time. Open, DefaultOpen and OnOpenChange are the usual controlled and uncontrolled pair. Close the dialog from inside with a button whose handler asks for it through OnOpenChange, or with the state you control.

A dialog that asks for a decision and must not close by a press outside is an [`AlertDialog`](#type-alertdialog).

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"), kit.Dialog{
        Trigger:     kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Children: h.Text("Edit profile")},
        Title:       h.Text("Edit profile"),
        Description: h.Text("Make changes to your profile here."),
        Children:    kit.Input{Placeholder: "Name"},
        Footer:      kit.Button{Children: h.Text("Save changes")},
    })
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Edit profile"))
fmt.Println("open:", app.Count(telatest.ByRole("dialog", "Edit profile")) == 1)
app.Press("Escape")
fmt.Println("open:", app.Count(telatest.ByRole("dialog", "Edit profile")) == 1)
// Output:
// open: true
// open: false
```

**Example (controlled)**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
open := true
// A controlled dialog shows the state it is given and reports what the
// user asked for, here an Escape; the app decides whether it closes.
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, func() tela.Node {
    return h.Fragment(kit.Dialog{
        Open:         &open,
        OnOpenChange: func(next bool) { fmt.Println("asked to open:", next) },
        Title:        h.Text("Welcome"),
        Description:  h.Text("Controlled by the app's own state."),
    })
})
app.Press("Escape")
fmt.Println("still open:", app.Count(telatest.ByRole("dialog", "Welcome")) == 1)
// Output:
// asked to open: false
// still open: true
```

#### func (Dialog) Build

```go
func (d Dialog) Build() tela.Node
```

Build returns the trigger and the dialog's portal.

### type DialogStyle

```go
type DialogStyle struct {
    // Positioner is the layer over the window that holds the overlay and
    // the dialog and centers the dialog, leaving shadcn's 1rem of room on
    // each side (its max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)]).
    Positioner string
    // Overlay is the scrim behind the dialog, and OverlayExit the classes
    // it transitions to while the dialog closes.
    Overlay     string
    OverlayExit string
    // Root is the dialog panel, and Exit the classes it transitions to
    // while it closes (the reverse of its starting: classes).
    Root string
    Exit string
    // Header holds the title and the description; it is drawn when the
    // dialog has either.
    Header      string
    Title       string
    Description string
    Footer      string
    // Close is the button in the corner (unless HideClose) and CloseIcon its icon.
    Close     string
    CloseIcon string
}
```

DialogStyle is the recipe of [`Dialog`](#type-dialog) (shadcn/ui's DialogOverlay, DialogContent, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, DialogDescription, DialogFooter and the close button of DialogContent).

Root is the dialog element, the panel with the role. shadcn centers it with fixed top-\[50%\] left-\[50%\] and a translation; here the Positioner, a fixed layer over the window, centers it with flex, which gives the same box and lets the panel keep its own transform for the entrance.

### type DropdownMenu

```go
type DropdownMenu[K comparable] struct {
    // Trigger is the element that opens the menu.
    Trigger Trigger
    // Items are the entries of the menu, in order.
    Items []MenuItem[K]
    // OnSelect is called with the key of a plain item when it is chosen,
    // after the item's own OnSelect.
    OnSelect func(K)
    // Placement is the side of the trigger the menu opens on: "bottom"
    // (the default), "top", "left" or "right"; a Floating UI placement such
    // as "bottom-start" also works. Align is where it sits along that side:
    // "start", "center" (the default) or "end".
    Placement, Align string
    // Offset is the distance in pixels between the trigger and the menu;
    // zero is 4 and [NoOffset] puts them together.
    Offset float32
    // Disabled makes the trigger inert.
    Disabled bool
    // AriaLabel names the menu when the trigger's text is not enough; the
    // menu is otherwise named by its trigger.
    AriaLabel string
    // CheckIcon and RadioIcon replace the check of a checkbox item and the
    // dot of a radio item.
    CheckIcon, RadioIcon tela.Icon

    // Open points to the open state of a controlled menu; nil leaves it to
    // the component, which starts closed unless DefaultOpen is set.
    // OnOpenChange is called with the next state.
    Open         *bool
    DefaultOpen  bool
    OnOpenChange func(open bool)

    // Class is added after the recipe's Content classes, to the menu's
    // panel (the root element of a dropdown menu is its trigger, the app's).
    Class string
    // Props are more props for the panel element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

DropdownMenu is a menu of actions that opens from a button, shadcn/ui's DropdownMenu: a press on the trigger, or Enter, Space or ArrowDown (and ArrowUp for the last item) when it has the focus, opens it below; the arrow keys, Home and End move through the items, typing jumps to one, Enter, Space or a click chooses it and Escape closes it. It is built on aria.UseMenuTrigger, aria.UsePopover and aria.UseMenu. The page is inert while it is open (it is modal, as Radix's), and the focus returns to the trigger when it closes.

```go
kit.DropdownMenu[string]{
    Trigger: kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Children: h.Text("Open")},
    Align:   "start",
    Items: []kit.MenuItem[string]{
        {Kind: kit.MenuLabel, Label: "My account"},
        {Kind: kit.MenuSeparator},
        {Key: "profile", Label: "Profile", Shortcut: "⇧⌘P"},
        {Key: "billing", Label: "Billing", Shortcut: "⌘B"},
        {Kind: kit.MenuSeparator},
        {Key: "logout", Label: "Log out", Variant: kit.Destructive},
    },
    OnSelect: func(key string) { run(key) },
}
```

The items are \[MenuItem\]s: plain items with an icon, a shortcut and a destructive variant, checkbox items, radio groups, labels, separators and groups. There are no submenus yet (a known gap, ADR-141): a menu is one level.

The Trigger slot is a [`Trigger`](#type-trigger) (see there): a [`Button`](#type-button), or anything made one with [`TriggerFunc`](#type-triggerfunc). Open, DefaultOpen and OnOpenChange are the usual controlled and uncontrolled pair; the panel exists only while the menu is open. It opens on the side Placement says ("bottom" by default, "top", "left" or "right") and Align puts it along that side ("start", "center" or "end"; Radix's default is the center), 4 px away unless Offset says otherwise, and it flips and shifts to stay in the window; a menu taller than the room left scrolls.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
dark := true
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"), kit.DropdownMenu[string]{
        Trigger: kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Children: h.Text("Account")},
        Align:   "start",
        Items: []kit.MenuItem[string]{
            {Kind: kit.MenuLabel, Label: "My account"},
            {Kind: kit.MenuSeparator},
            {Key: "profile", Label: "Profile", Shortcut: "⇧⌘P"},
            {Kind: kit.MenuCheckbox, Key: "dark", Label: "Dark mode", Checked: &dark,
                OnCheckedChange: func(on bool) { dark = on }},
            {Kind: kit.MenuSeparator},
            {Key: "logout", Label: "Log out", Variant: kit.Destructive},
        },
        OnSelect: func(key string) { fmt.Println("chose", key) },
    })
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Account"))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("menuitem", "Profile"))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Account"))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("menuitemcheckbox", "Dark mode"))
fmt.Println("dark:", dark)
// Output:
// chose profile
// dark: false
```
