```go
func (d DropdownMenu[K]) Build() tela.Node
```

Build returns the trigger and the menu's portal.

### type Field

```go
type Field struct {
    // Label, Description and Error are plain text; empty draws nothing.
    Label, Description, Error string
    // Invalid makes the field invalid with no error message, such as when
    // the message is shown elsewhere. A field with an Error is invalid
    // already.
    Invalid bool
    // Orientation is Vertical (the zero value) or Horizontal.
    Orientation Orientation
    // ControlAfter puts the control after the label and the description, as
    // in shadcn's switch rows (FieldContent first, then the Switch). It only
    // affects a Horizontal field: a Vertical one is always the label, the
    // control, the description and the error. The DOM order, and so the
    // reading order of a screen reader, is the visual one; the label still
    // points to the control, and the error and the invalid state still reach
    // it.
    ControlAfter bool
    // Children is the control.
    Children tela.Component

    // Class is added after the recipe's Root classes. The other Class
    // fields do the same for their part.
    Class            string
    LabelClass       string
    ContentClass     string
    DescriptionClass string
    ErrorClass       string
    // Props are more props for the root element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

Field is a form control with its label, its help text and its error, shadcn/ui's Field. It does the wiring: the label points to the control (the control takes an id made with tela.UseID and the label's For is the same), and the control is described by the error when there is one, else by the description. The control is the Children, an [`Input`](#type-input) or a [`Textarea`](#type-textarea) (more controls of the kit take the id the same way as they arrive).

```go
kit.Field{
    Label:       "Email",
    Description: "We never share it.",
    Error:       errs.Email, // empty: no error
    Children:    kit.Input{Type: "email", Value: &email, OnValueChange: setEmail.Set},
}
```

The error shows as an alert below the control, and the field is invalid while it shows one: the control is marked h.AriaInvalid (a red border and ring from the recipe's aria-invalid: classes) and the label turns red.

A Horizontal field puts the control before its text, as shadcn does for a checkbox or a radio. A switch row has the text first: set ControlAfter.

```go
kit.Field{
    Orientation:  kit.Horizontal,
    ControlAfter: true,
    Label:        "Marketing emails",
    Description:  "News about new features and offers.",
    Class:        "items-center gap-6",
    Children:     kit.Switch{Checked: &on, OnCheckedChange: setOn.Set},
}
```

To name a group of controls (a [`RadioGroup`](#type-radiogroup), a [`ToggleGroup`](#type-togglegroup)) use a [`FieldSet`](#type-fieldset) and its legend: a Field's label points to one control.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
app := telatest.Mount(t, emailForm{})
app.Fill(telatest.ByRole("textbox", "Email"), "ana@example.com")
app.ExpectValue(telatest.ByRole("textbox", "Email"), "ana@example.com")
fmt.Println("the label names the input")
// Output: the label names the input
```

#### func (Field) Build

```go
func (f Field) Build() tela.Node
```

Build returns the field element: a group holding the label, the control, the description and the error.

### type FieldSet

```go
type FieldSet struct {
    // Legend is the caption of the group, plain text; empty draws none.
    Legend string
    // LegendVariant is [LegendVariantLegend] (the zero value, a title) or
    // [LegendVariantLabel] (a caption the size of a field's label).
    LegendVariant LegendVariant
    // Description is help text under the legend; empty draws none.
    Description string
    // Children are the controls, laid out in a column.
    Children tela.Component

    // Class is added after the recipe's Root classes. The other Class
    // fields do the same for their part; ContentClass is for the column of
    // the description and the children (set its gap here).
    Class            string
    LegendClass      string
    DescriptionClass string
    ContentClass     string
    // Props are more props for the root element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

FieldSet is a group of controls with a caption, shadcn/ui's FieldSet with its FieldLegend and FieldDescription. It is a group (role "group") named by the legend and described by the description. A [`RadioGroup`](#type-radiogroup) or a [`ToggleGroup`](#type-togglegroup) inside it takes its name from the legend, so it needs no AriaLabel and no [`Label`](#type-label) that points at nothing; a group of its own AriaLabel keeps it.

```go
kit.FieldSet{
    Legend:        "Theme",
    LegendVariant: kit.LegendVariantLabel,
    Description:   "Pick how the app looks.", // optional
    Children: kit.RadioGroup[string]{Items: themes, Value: &theme, OnValueChange: setTheme.Set},
}
```

The children are laid out in a column with a gap of 24 px (12 px for a RadioGroup given directly as Children, as in shadcn). Give several as h.Fragment, such as a few \[Field\]s:

```go
kit.FieldSet{Legend: "Address", Description: "Where we send the invoice.",
    Children: h.Fragment(
        kit.Field{Label: "Street", Children: kit.Input{}},
        kit.Field{Label: "City", Children: kit.Input{}})}
```

shadcn's FieldGroup, the column that stacks fields with a 28 px gap, has no component: a FieldSet is already a column, and for any other place h.Div(h.Class("flex w-full flex-col gap-7"), ...) is the same.

The legend is a block above the children whose margin (mb-3) separates it from them; the description is pulled up under a legend of the default variant (-mt-1.5). shadcn's nth-last-2:-mt-1, which pulls a description that has exactly one item after it, is not applied to the label variant: add -mt-1 to DescriptionClass for it.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
plan := "free"
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"),
        kit.FieldSet{Legend: "Plan", LegendVariant: kit.LegendVariantLabel,
            Children: kit.RadioGroup[string]{Items: plans, Value: &plan, OnValueChange: func(k string) { plan = k }}})
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("radio", "Pro"))
fmt.Println("plan", plan)
// Output: plan pro
```

#### func (FieldSet) Build

```go
func (f FieldSet) Build() tela.Node
```

Build returns the group element: the legend, then the description and the children in a column.

### type FieldSetStyle

```go
type FieldSetStyle struct {
    // Root is the group: the legend and, under it, the column of parts. A
    // fieldset is a block, and its legend is not one of the column's items,
    // so the legend's margin alone separates the two (as in a browser).
    Root string
    // Content is the column that holds the description and the children
    // (shadcn's fieldset: flex flex-col gap-6).
    Content string
    // ContentWithRadioGroup is added to Content when the children are a
    // [RadioGroup] (shadcn's has-[>[data-slot=radio-group]]:gap-3).
    ContentWithRadioGroup string
    // Legend is the legend's classes. It has w-fit because a browser's
    // legend is as wide as its text.
    Legend string
    // LegendVariants are the sizes of the legend.
    LegendVariants map[LegendVariant]string
    // Description is the help text under the legend.
    Description string
    // DescriptionAfterLegend is added to Description for each legend
    // variant that pulls the description up under it (shadcn's
    // [[data-variant=legend]+&]:-mt-1.5, which only the legend variant has).
    DescriptionAfterLegend map[LegendVariant]string
}
```

FieldSetStyle is the recipe of [`FieldSet`](#type-fieldset) (shadcn/ui's FieldSet, FieldLegend and FieldDescription).

### type FieldStyle

```go
type FieldStyle struct {
    Root string
    // Orientations are the arrangement of the control and its text:
    // Vertical (the label above the control) and Horizontal (the control
    // first, then the text; the text first with Field.ControlAfter).
    Orientations map[Orientation]string
    // HorizontalWithContent is added to Root when a Horizontal field has a
    // Content part (shadcn's has-[>[data-slot=field-content]]:).
    HorizontalWithContent string
    // Label is added to the [Label] recipe's classes for the field's label.
    Label string
    // HorizontalLabel is added to Label when a Horizontal field has no
    // Content part and the label sits next to the control.
    HorizontalLabel string
    // Content holds the label, description and error of a Horizontal
    // field that has a description or an error.
    Content     string
    Description string
    // DescriptionWithError is added to Description when the field shows an
    // error below it (shadcn's nth-last-2:).
    DescriptionWithError string
    // Invalid is added to Root when the field is invalid (shadcn's
    // data-[invalid=true]:): the label and the text turn red.
    Invalid string
    Error   string
}
```

FieldStyle is the recipe of [`Field`](#type-field) (shadcn/ui's Field, FieldLabel, FieldContent, FieldDescription and FieldError).

### type Input

```go
type Input struct {
    // Value points to the text of a controlled field; nil leaves the text
    // to the field, which starts with DefaultValue.
    Value *string
    // DefaultValue is the initial text of an uncontrolled field.
    DefaultValue string
    // OnValueChange is called with the new text after every edit. For a
    // controlled field it is how the change is asked for.
    OnValueChange func(string)
    // Type is "text" (the default), "password", "email", "search", "url",
    // "tel" or "number" (h.Type).
    Type        string
    Placeholder string
    // Name names the field in its h.Form.
    Name string
    // ID is the field's id, for a [Label]'s For. Inside a [Field] it
    // defaults to the field's.
    ID string
    // AriaLabel names a field that has no label of its own, such as a
    // search box; a [Field]'s Label or a [Label] pointing to the field
    // names it otherwise.
    AriaLabel string
    Disabled  bool
    ReadOnly  bool
    // Invalid marks the value as wrong: assistive technologies announce it
    // and the recipe's aria-invalid: classes (a red border and ring) apply.
    // A [Field] with an Error sets it on its control.
    Invalid   bool
    AutoFocus bool
    // MaxLength limits what the user can type, in UTF-16 code units; 0 is
    // no limit.
    MaxLength int
    // Class is added after the recipe's classes.
    Class string
    // Props are more props for the input element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

Input is a single-line text field, shadcn/ui's Input. Its value follows the controlled and uncontrolled rule of the whole kit: give Value (a pointer to the state) and OnValueChange to keep the value yourself, or DefaultValue to let the field keep it.

```go
name, setName := tela.UseState("")
kit.Input{Placeholder: "Name", Value: &name, OnValueChange: setName.Set}

kit.Input{Type: "email", DefaultValue: "ana@example.com", Name: "email"}
```

Inside a [`Field`](#type-field) the input takes the field's ID, so the field's label names it, and is described by the field's description or error.


```go
type InputStyle struct {
    Root string
}
```

InputStyle is the recipe of [`Input`](#type-input) (shadcn/ui's Input).

### type Label

```go
type Label struct {
    // For is the ID of the control the label names (h.For).
    For string
    // Disabled dims the label and makes it ignore the pointer; a control
    // that is a sibling after a label with the class "peer" dims it with
    // peer-disabled: without it.
    Disabled bool
    // Children is the text.
    Children tela.Component
    // Class is added after the recipe's classes.
    Class string
    // Props are more props for the label element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

Label is the caption of a form control, shadcn/ui's Label. Clicking it focuses the control it labels, which also gets its accessible name from it. It labels the control whose ID is its For, or else the field or button inside it.

```go
kit.Label{For: "email", Children: h.Text("Email")}
kit.Input{ID: "email", Type: "email"}
```

A [`Field`](#type-field) wires a label and its control with no ids to write.

### type LegendVariant

```go
type LegendVariant string
```

LegendVariant is the look of a [`FieldSet`](#type-fieldset)'s legend (shadcn's FieldLegend variant): the size of its text. Like [`Variant`](#type-variant) it is open: an app adds a variant by naming it in the recipe's LegendVariants map.

```go
const (
    // LegendVariantLegend is the default: a title, text-base. The zero
    // value is the same variant.
    LegendVariantLegend LegendVariant = "legend"
    // LegendVariantLabel is a caption for a group of controls, text-sm, as
    // a [Field]'s label is.
    LegendVariantLabel LegendVariant = "label"
)
```

### type MenuItem

```go
type MenuItem[K comparable] struct {
    // Kind is what the entry is; the zero value is a plain item.
    Kind MenuKind
    // Key identifies a plain, checkbox or radio item, and a radio group.
    Key K
    // Label is the item's text, a label's text, or a group's accessible name.
    Label string
    // Icon is drawn before the label of a plain item.
    Icon tela.Icon
    // Shortcut is text shown at the end of the item, such as "⌘T". It is
    // only shown: binding the keys is the app's.
    Shortcut string
    // Variant is Default or Destructive (a plain item, as shadcn's
    // variant="destructive").
    Variant Variant
    // Disabled makes the item (for a radio group or a group, all of its
    // items) impossible to choose.
    Disabled bool
    // Inset pads a plain item or a label like the ones with a check or an
    // icon, so that their texts line up (shadcn's inset).
    Inset bool
    // KeepOpen keeps the menu open when this item is chosen, such as a
    // checkbox toggled in a row.
    KeepOpen bool
    // OnSelect is called when a plain item is chosen.
    OnSelect func()

    // Checked points to the state of a controlled checkbox item; nil leaves
    // it to the menu, which starts at DefaultChecked. OnCheckedChange is
    // called with the next state.
    Checked         *bool
    DefaultChecked  bool
    OnCheckedChange func(checked bool)

    // Value points to the chosen item of a controlled radio group; nil
    // leaves it to the menu, which starts at DefaultValue (an item whose
    // Key it equals; nil: none chosen, a pointer so that the zero K can be
    // a key). OnValueChange is called with the Key of the item the user
    // chose.
    Value         *K
    DefaultValue  *K
    OnValueChange func(K)

    // Items are the radio items of a radio group, or the entries of a
    // group.
    Items []MenuItem[K]

    // Class is added after the recipe's classes, to the item.
    Class string
}
```

MenuItem is one entry of a menu, whatever its kind: the model that [`DropdownMenu`](#type-dropdownmenu), [`Menubar`](#type-menubar) and [`ContextMenu`](#type-contextmenu) share. K is the type of the keys, which name the items that can be chosen. A menu is a slice of them:

```go
[]kit.MenuItem[string]{
    {Kind: kit.MenuLabel, Label: "My account"},
    {Key: "profile", Label: "Profile", Shortcut: "⇧⌘P", OnSelect: openProfile},
    {Key: "billing", Label: "Billing"},
    {Kind: kit.MenuSeparator},
    {Kind: kit.MenuCheckbox, Key: "bars", Label: "Status bar", DefaultChecked: true},
    {Kind: kit.MenuSeparator},
    {Kind: kit.MenuRadioGroup, Key: "theme", DefaultValue: new("light"), Items: []kit.MenuItem[string]{
        {Key: "light", Label: "Light"}, {Key: "dark", Label: "Dark"}}},
    {Key: "logout", Label: "Log out", Variant: kit.Destructive},
}
```

Every item that can be chosen (a plain item, a checkbox item, a radio item) needs a Key distinct from the others of its menu; it is what the menu's OnSelect reports and what the keyboard's typeahead and the accessibility tree tell items apart by. A menu with two items of the same Key panics in dev mode. Fields that a kind does not use are ignored.

Choosing a plain item calls its OnSelect and the menu's, and closes the menu; a checkbox item toggles and a radio item chooses, and they close the menu too (Radix's default) unless KeepOpen is set. A disabled item is skipped by the keyboard and dimmed.

Checkbox items and radio groups follow the kit's value rule: Checked (a pointer to your state) with OnCheckedChange controls a checkbox item, DefaultChecked starts an uncontrolled one; Value with OnValueChange controls a radio group, DefaultValue starts one. An uncontrolled state is kept by the menu component, so it survives the menu closing and opening.

### type MenuKind

```go
type MenuKind int
```

MenuKind is what a [`MenuItem`](#type-menuitem) is: an item that does something, a checkbox item, a group of radio items, a label, a separator or a group.

```go
const (
    // MenuPlain is an item that does something when it is chosen
    // (shadcn's DropdownMenuItem): Key, Label, Icon, Shortcut, Variant,
    // Disabled, Inset, OnSelect.
    MenuPlain MenuKind = iota
    // MenuCheckbox is an item that is on or off (DropdownMenuCheckboxItem):
    // Key, Label, Shortcut, Disabled and Checked/DefaultChecked/
    // OnCheckedChange.
    MenuCheckbox
    // MenuRadioGroup is a set of exclusive items (DropdownMenuRadioGroup
    // with its RadioItems): Key names the group and Items are the radio
    // items, whose Key is their value. Value/DefaultValue/OnValueChange say
    // which is chosen.
    MenuRadioGroup
    // MenuLabel is a heading (DropdownMenuLabel): Label and Inset.
    MenuLabel
    // MenuSeparator is a line between items (DropdownMenuSeparator).
    MenuSeparator
    // MenuGroup gathers Items under the role "group" (DropdownMenuGroup);
    // Label, when set, is its accessible name (it is not drawn: put a
    // MenuLabel in Items for a visible heading).
    MenuGroup
)
```

The kinds of [`MenuItem`](#type-menuitem). MenuPlain is the zero value, so an item that only has a Key and a Label is an ordinary one.

### type MenuStyle

```go
type MenuStyle struct {
    // Content is the panel: surface, border, shadow, padding, its minimum
    // width and the entrance. It scrolls when there is no room for it.
    Content string
    // Exit is what the panel transitions to as it closes.
    Exit string
    // Sides adds classes for the side of the trigger the panel is on
    // ("top", "right", "bottom" or "left"): the transform origin and the
    // slide it enters with, as [PopoverStyle].Sides.
    Sides map[string]string
    // Item is a plain item, ItemVariants adds the classes of a Variant
    // (Destructive, and the empty key for the default), ItemInset the
    // padding of an inset item.
    Item         string
    ItemVariants map[Variant]string
    ItemInset    string
    // ItemIcon is the icon of a plain item and ItemIconVariants its color
    // per Variant.
    ItemIcon         string
    ItemIconVariants map[Variant]string
    // CheckboxItem and RadioItem are the items with an indicator at the
    // start; Indicator is the box that holds it, CheckIcon the check and
    // RadioIcon the dot.
    CheckboxItem string
    RadioItem    string
    Indicator    string
    CheckIcon    string
    RadioIcon    string
    // Label is a heading, LabelInset its padding when inset.
    Label      string
    LabelInset string
    // Separator is the line between items.
    Separator string
    // Shortcut is the text at the end of an item.
    Shortcut string
}
```

MenuStyle is the recipe of the panel of a menu and its items, shared by [`DropdownMenu`](#type-dropdownmenu) and [`ContextMenu`](#type-contextmenu) (shadcn/ui's DropdownMenuContent and ContextMenuContent and what they hold) and used by [`Menubar`](#type-menubar) for its menus.

### type Menubar

```go
type Menubar[K comparable] struct {
    // Menus are the bar's menus, in order.
    Menus []MenubarMenu[K]
    // OnSelect is called with the key of the menu and of the plain item
    // that was chosen, after the item's own OnSelect.
    OnSelect func(menu, item K)
    // AriaLabel names the bar.
    AriaLabel string
    // Direction is "ltr" or "rtl"; empty is the direction at the component's
    // position (tela.UseDirection: the nearest h.Dir above it, left to right
    // without one). Under "rtl" ArrowLeft goes to the next menu and ArrowRight to the previous one; a Direction given here also
    // sets the direction of the layout.
    Direction string
    // CheckIcon and RadioIcon replace the check of a checkbox item and the
    // dot of a radio item.
    CheckIcon, RadioIcon tela.Icon

    // Open points to the open menu of a controlled bar; nil leaves it to
    // the component, which starts with DefaultOpen (nil: all closed).
    // OnOpenChange is called with the menu that opens (open true) or the one
    // that closes; moving from one menu to another is one call, with the one
    // that opens.
    Open         *K
    DefaultOpen  *K
    OnOpenChange func(menu K, open bool)

    // Class is added after the recipe's Root classes, to the bar;
    // TriggerClass does the same for the menus' buttons and ContentClass for
    // the menus' panels.
    Class        string
    TriggerClass string
    ContentClass string
    // Props are more props for the bar element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

Menubar is a row of menus, such as the File, Edit and View of an application, shadcn/ui's Menubar, built on aria.UseMenuBar: the bar is one tab stop, ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move between the menus' buttons (and, with a menu open, open the neighbor's), Home and End jump, ArrowDown, Enter and Space open the menu on its first item and ArrowUp on its last; once a menu is open, hovering another button opens that one. A press on the open menu's button, Escape, a press outside and Tab close it.

```go
kit.Menubar[string]{
    AriaLabel: "Application",
    Menus: []kit.MenubarMenu[string]{
        {Key: "file", Label: "File", Items: []kit.MenuItem[string]{
            {Key: "new", Label: "New Tab", Shortcut: "⌘T"},
            {Key: "window", Label: "New Window", Shortcut: "⌘N"},
            {Kind: kit.MenuSeparator},
            {Key: "print", Label: "Print...", Shortcut: "⌘P"},
        }},
        {Key: "edit", Label: "Edit", Items: edit},
    },
    OnSelect: func(menu, item string) { run(menu, item) },
}
```

The items are the \[MenuItem\]s of [`DropdownMenu`](#type-dropdownmenu), with no submenus yet (ADR-141). The keys of the menus and of the items have the same type K; an item key needs to be distinct only within its menu. The open menu follows the kit's value rule with Open (a pointer to the key of the open menu; a key no menu has, such as the zero K, means all closed), DefaultOpen and OnOpenChange.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"), kit.Menubar[string]{
        AriaLabel: "Application",
        Menus: []kit.MenubarMenu[string]{
            {Key: "file", Label: "File", Items: []kit.MenuItem[string]{
                {Key: "new", Label: "New Tab", Shortcut: "⌘T"},
                {Kind: kit.MenuSeparator},
                {Key: "print", Label: "Print...", Shortcut: "⌘P"},
            }},
            {Key: "edit", Label: "Edit", Items: []kit.MenuItem[string]{
                {Key: "undo", Label: "Undo", Shortcut: "⌘Z"},
            }},
        },
        OnSelect: func(menu, item string) { fmt.Println(menu, item) },
    })
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("menuitem", "File"))
// With a menu open, hovering another button opens its menu.
app.Hover(telatest.ByRole("menuitem", "Edit"))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("menuitem", "Undo"))
// Output: edit undo
```


```go
    Key K
    // Label is the text of the menu's button in the bar.
    Label string
    // Disabled makes the menu impossible to open.

    // Items are the entries of the menu.
```

```go
    // Trigger is a menu's button in the bar; aria-expanded: styles the one
    // whose menu is open.

    // Menu is the recipe of the menus and their items.

}
```

```go
type Orientation string
```

Orientation is the direction a component lays its parts out in. The zero value is the component's own default: Horizontal for a [`Separator`](#type-separator), Vertical for a [`Field`](#type-field).

```go
const (
    Horizontal Orientation = "horizontal"
    Vertical   Orientation = "vertical"
```

### type Popover

```go
type Popover struct {
    // Trigger is the element the popover is anchored to and that opens it.
    Trigger Trigger
    // Children is the content of the panel.
    Children tela.Component
    // Placement is the side of the trigger the panel opens on: "bottom"
    // (the default), "top", "left" or "right"; a Floating UI placement such
    // as "bottom-start" also works. Align is where it sits along that side:
    // "start", "center" (the default) or "end".
    Placement, Align string
    // Offset is the distance in pixels between the trigger and the panel;
    // zero is 4 and [NoOffset] puts them together.
    Offset float32
    // Modal makes the rest of the window inert while the popover is open,
    // as a dialog does. The default is a popover that leaves the page
    // usable.
    Modal bool
    // AriaLabel names the panel (it is a dialog for assistive technologies).
    AriaLabel string

    // Open points to the open state of a controlled popover; nil leaves the
    // state to the popover, which starts closed unless DefaultOpen is set.
    // OnOpenChange is called with the next state when the trigger, Escape or
    // a press outside asks for a change.
    Open         *bool
    DefaultOpen  bool
    OnOpenChange func(open bool)
    // Disabled disables the trigger, which is then inert and dimmed by its
    // recipe; the popover does not open. Set it here: the trigger props
    // override a Disabled given to the trigger component itself.
    Disabled bool

    // Class is added after the recipe's Root classes, to the panel.
    Class string
    // Props are more props for the panel element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

Popover is a panel anchored to its trigger, shadcn/ui's Popover: it opens next to the trigger, scales and fades in, and closes with Escape, a press outside it or the focus moving elsewhere. It does not block the page (it is not modal): the rest of the window stays in the accessibility tree and can take the focus. The press that closes it is not delivered to what is under it, as in React Aria. The focus moves into the panel when it opens and returns to the trigger when it closes. A press on the trigger toggles it.

```go
kit.Popover{
    Trigger:   kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Children: h.Text("Dimensions")},
    Placement: "bottom", Align: "start",
    Children:  dimensionsForm,
}
```

The Trigger slot is a [`Trigger`](#type-trigger): a [`Button`](#type-button), or anything made one with [`TriggerFunc`](#type-triggerfunc). The panel is placed with Floating UI's algorithm: it flips to the other side when there is no room and shifts to stay in the window. Open, DefaultOpen and OnOpenChange are the usual controlled and uncontrolled pair; the panel exists only while it is open.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"), kit.Popover{
        Trigger:   kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Children: h.Text("Dimensions")},
        Placement: "bottom", Align: "start",
        AriaLabel: "Dimensions",
        Children:  h.P(h.Text("Set the dimensions for the layer.")),
    })
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
trigger := telatest.ByRole("button", "Dimensions")
app.Click(trigger)
fmt.Println("open:", app.Count(telatest.ByRole("dialog", "Dimensions")) == 1)
app.Click(trigger) // the trigger toggles it
fmt.Println("open:", app.Count(telatest.ByRole("dialog", "Dimensions")) == 1)
// Output:
// open: true
// open: false
```

```go
func (p Popover) Build() tela.Node
```

Build returns the trigger and the popover's portal.

```go
type PopoverStyle struct {
    // Root is the panel: surface, border, shadow, padding and the

    Root string
    // Exit is what the panel transitions to as it closes.
    Exit string
    // Sides adds classes for the side of the trigger the panel is on
    // ("top", "right", "bottom" or "left"): the transform origin of the
    // entrance, which scales out of the trigger's edge, and the slide of
    // 0.5rem it starts from (shadcn's data-[side=bottom]:slide-in-from-top-2
    // and the like).
    Sides map[string]string
}
```

PopoverStyle is the recipe of [`Popover`](#type-popover) (shadcn/ui's PopoverContent).

### type Progress

```go
type Progress struct {
    // Value is how far the task is, from 0 to Max.
    Value float64
    // Max is the value of a finished task (100 by default).
    Max float64
    // Indeterminate says that the amount of progress is unknown: the bar
    // has no value and pulses.
    Indeterminate bool
    // FormatValue returns Value as people read it (aria-valuetext); the
    // default is the percentage, "40%".
    FormatValue func(float64) string
    // AriaLabel names the bar.
    AriaLabel string
    // Class is added after the recipe's classes; IndicatorClass does the
    // same for the bar.
    Class          string
    IndicatorClass string
    // Props are more props for the track element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

Progress is a bar that shows how far a task is, shadcn/ui's Progress, on aria.UseProgressBar: it has the progressbar role, its range and aria-valuenow, and the bar moves with a transition when Value changes.

```go
kit.Progress{Value: uploaded, AriaLabel: "Upload"} // 0 to 100

kit.Progress{Value: 512, Max: 2048, FormatValue: func(v float64) string { return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f MB", v) }}
```

Use Indeterminate while the amount is unknown. For a measure that is not the progress of a task, such as disk usage, use aria.UseMeter.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("w-64 p-6"), kit.Progress{Value: 40, AriaLabel: "Upload"})
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.ExpectRole("progressbar", "Upload")
fmt.Println("progress shown")
// Output: progress shown
```


```go
    // Indicator is the bar; it is as wide as the track and moves toward the

    // rtl: class the component adds) by the part that is not done.
    Indicator string
    // Indeterminate is added to the indicator while the amount of progress

    Indeterminate string
}
```

### type RadioGroup

```go
type RadioGroup[K comparable] struct {
    // Items are the options, in order.
    Items []RadioItem[K]
    // Value points to the checked key of a controlled group; nil leaves it
    // to the group, which starts at DefaultValue (nil: nothing checked).
    Value        *K
    DefaultValue *K
    // OnValueChange is called with the next key when the user checks an
    // option. For a controlled group it is how the change is asked for.
    OnValueChange func(K)
    // Orientation is Vertical (the default) or Horizontal; it is the
    // group's aria-orientation and the arrangement of the options.
    Orientation Orientation
    // Direction is "ltr" or "rtl"; empty is the direction at the component's
    // position (tela.UseDirection: the nearest h.Dir above it, left to right
    // without one). Under "rtl" ArrowLeft goes to the next option and ArrowRight to the previous one; a Direction given here also
    // sets the direction of the layout.
    Direction string
    // Disabled disables every option.
    Disabled bool
    // ReadOnly keeps the options focusable but not changeable.
    ReadOnly bool
    // Required marks the group as one the user must answer.
    Required bool
    // Invalid marks the group wrong: the circles take the invalid look. A
    // [Field] with an Error sets it.
    Invalid bool
    // AriaLabel names the group; without it a [FieldSet]'s legend does.
    AriaLabel string
    // Render draws one option in place of the default (circle, label and
    // description); see [RadioState]. It runs while the group builds.
    Render func(item RadioItem[K], state RadioState) tela.Node
    // Class is added after the recipe's classes. OptionClass, ItemClass,
    // LabelClass and DescriptionClass do the same for their parts of the
    // default look.
    Class            string
    OptionClass      string
    ItemClass        string
    LabelClass       string
    DescriptionClass string
    // Props are more props for the group element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

RadioGroup is a set of options of which one is chosen, shadcn/ui's RadioGroup, on aria.UseRadioGroup: the arrow keys (all four) move the focus to the next option and check it, Space checks, and Tab enters the group at the checked option. The value follows the kit's rule for a choice among keys: Value (a pointer to the key), DefaultValue and OnValueChange; nothing is checked while there is no value.

```go
plan, setPlan := tela.UseState("pro")
kit.RadioGroup[string]{
    AriaLabel: "Plan", Value: &plan, OnValueChange: setPlan.Set,
    Items: []kit.RadioItem[string]{
        {Value: "free", Label: "Free"},
        {Value: "pro", Label: "Pro", Description: "For small teams."},
    },
}
```

To draw the options yourself, such as theme cards, give Render: it is called for each option with the state and the props of its radio, and the group keeps the behavior.

```go
kit.RadioGroup[string]{AriaLabel: "Theme", DefaultValue: new("light"), Orientation: kit.Horizontal,
    Items: themes, Render: func(it kit.RadioItem[string], st kit.RadioState) tela.Node {
        return h.Button(st.Props, cls("rounded-lg border p-4 aria-checked:border-primary"),
            h.Text(it.Label))
    }}
```

Inside a [`Field`](#type-field) the group takes the field's description and invalid state. Name it with AriaLabel, or put it in a [`FieldSet`](#type-fieldset) whose Legend names it.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
plan := "free"
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"), kit.RadioGroup[string]{
        AriaLabel: "Plan", DefaultValue: &plan, OnValueChange: func(k string) { plan = k },
        Items: []kit.RadioItem[string]{
            {Value: "free", Label: "Free"},
            {Value: "pro", Label: "Pro", Description: "For small teams."},
        }})
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("radio", "Pro"))
fmt.Println("plan", plan)
// Output: plan pro
```


Build returns the group element.

```go
type RadioGroupStyle struct {
    // Root is the group: the options in a grid.
    Root string
    // Orientations are the arrangement of the options: Vertical (a column)
    // and Horizontal (a row).
    Orientations map[Orientation]string
    // Option is the row of one option: the circle and its text.
    Option string
    // OptionWithDescription is added to an option that has a Description:
    // the circle sits at the top, beside the text.
    OptionWithDescription string
    // Item is the radio circle (shadcn's RadioGroupItem): size, border,

    Item string

    // Description (shadcn's mt-px of a Field's radio).
    ItemWithDescription string

    Indicator string
    // Icon is the dot.
    Icon string
    // Label is added to the [Label] recipe's classes for an option's label.
    Label string
    // LabelWithDescription is added to Label when the option has a
    // Description (a [Field]'s label: snug leading).
    LabelWithDescription string
    // Content holds the label and the description of an option that has a
    // Description.
    Content string
    // Description is the help text under an option's label.
    Description string
}
```

RadioGroupStyle is the recipe of [`RadioGroup`](#type-radiogroup) (shadcn/ui's RadioGroup and RadioGroupItem, with the label arrangement of its documentation and of [`Field`](#type-field)).

```go
type RadioState struct {
    // Checked is whether the option is the group's value.
    Checked bool
    // Disabled is whether the option, or the whole group, is disabled.
    Disabled bool
    // Invalid is whether the group is invalid.
    Invalid bool
    // ID is the id of the radio element, for a [Label]'s For.

    Props tela.Prop

    Indicator tela.Component
}
```

### type RangeCalendar

```go
type RangeCalendar struct {
    // Value points to the selected range of a controlled calendar; nil
    // leaves it to the calendar, which starts at DefaultValue.
    Value        *aria.DateRange
    DefaultValue aria.DateRange
    // OnValueChange is called with the range the user completes.
    OnValueChange func(aria.DateRange)
    // AllowsNonContiguousRanges lets a range cross unavailable dates.
    AllowsNonContiguousRanges bool

    Min, Max                 aria.Date
    IsDateUnavailable        func(aria.Date) bool
    Disabled, ReadOnly       bool
    FocusedDate              *aria.Date
    DefaultFocusedDate       aria.Date
    OnFocusChange            func(aria.Date)
    VisibleMonths            int
    FirstDayOfWeek           *time.Weekday
    FixedWeeks               bool
    HideOutsideDays          bool
    NarrowWeekdays           bool
    Today                    aria.Date
    Locale, Direction        string
    AriaLabel                string
    PreviousLabel, NextLabel string
    PreviousIcon, NextIcon   tela.Icon

    Class          string
    MonthsClass    string
    MonthClass     string
    NavClass       string
    CaptionClass   string
    WeekdayClass   string
    DayClass       string
    DayButtonClass string
    Props          tela.Child
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

RangeCalendar is a [`Calendar`](#type-calendar) that selects a span of dates, shadcn/ui's Calendar in range mode on aria.UseRangeCalendar. Selecting takes two presses: the first anchors the range, the pointer over a date or the focus on it previews the range up to it (the band of accent color between the two ends), and the second completes it, the earlier date first. Escape cancels an anchored range. While one is anchored, dates beyond the nearest unavailable one are not selectable, unless AllowsNonContiguousRanges.

```go
var stay aria.DateRange
kit.RangeCalendar{VisibleMonths: 2, OnValueChange: func(r aria.DateRange) { stay = r }}
```

The value follows the kit's rule with aria.DateRange: Value (a pointer) with OnValueChange controls it, DefaultValue starts an uncontrolled one; OnValueChange is called when a range is completed, not when it is anchored. The other fields are those of [`Calendar`](#type-calendar).

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
var stay aria.DateRange
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"), kit.RangeCalendar{
        Today:         aria.Date{Year: 2026, Month: time.October, Day: 25},
        VisibleMonths: 2,
        OnValueChange: func(r aria.DateRange) { stay = r },
    })
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page, telatest.Size(800, 400))
// The first press anchors the range, the second completes it.
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("gridcell", "Tuesday, October 27, 2026"))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("gridcell", "Thursday, November 5, 2026"))
fmt.Println(stay.Start, stay.End)
// Output: 2026-10-27 2026-11-05
```

```go
func (c RangeCalendar) Build() tela.Node
```

### type Select

```go
type Select[K comparable] struct {
    // Items are the options, in order.
    Items []SelectItem[K]
    // Value points to the chosen option of a controlled Select; nil leaves
    // the choice to the component, which starts at DefaultValue.
    Value *K
    // DefaultValue points to the option an uncontrolled Select starts with;
    // nil starts with nothing chosen.
    DefaultValue *K
    // OnValueChange is called with the key of the option the user chose. For
    // a controlled Select it is how the change is asked for.
    OnValueChange func(K)
    // Open points to the open state of a controlled list; nil leaves it to
    // the component, which starts at DefaultOpen. OnOpenChange is called with
    // the next state.
    Open         *bool
    DefaultOpen  bool
    OnOpenChange func(open bool)
    // Placeholder is shown while nothing is chosen.
    Placeholder string
    // Size is Default (36 px) or Sm (32 px).
    Size Size
    // Disabled makes the select inert and dims it.
    Disabled bool
    // Invalid marks the choice as wrong: assistive technologies announce it
    // and the recipe's aria-invalid: classes (a red border and ring) apply.
    // A [Field] with an Error sets it.
    Invalid bool
    // ID is the trigger's id, for a [Label]'s For. Inside a [Field] it
    // defaults to the field's.
    ID string
    // AriaLabel names the select when no label is tied to it; inside a Field
    // with a Label that label is used.
    AriaLabel string
    // Icon replaces the chevron at the end of the trigger, CheckIcon the
    // check that marks the chosen option.
    Icon, CheckIcon tela.Icon

    // Class is added after the recipe's Root classes (the trigger's); the
    // other Class fields do the same for their part: the popover, an item,
    // and a group's label.
    Class        string
    ContentClass string
    ItemClass    string
    LabelClass   string
    // Props are more props for the trigger element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

Select is a dropdown that picks one of a list of options, shadcn/ui's Select: a trigger that shows the chosen option and a popover list that opens below it. It is built on aria.UseSelect: a press, Enter, Space and the arrow keys open the list, the arrows and Home and End move through it, typing jumps to an option, Enter or a click chooses it, and Escape closes it. On the closed trigger, typing and the left and right arrows choose without opening.

```go
kit.Select[string]{
    Placeholder: "Select a fruit",
    Items: []kit.SelectItem[string]{
        {Value: "apple", Label: "Apple"},
        {Value: "banana", Label: "Banana"},
        {Value: "grape", Label: "Grape", Disabled: true},
    },
    OnValueChange: func(v string) { fmt.Println("chose", v) },
}
```

The chosen option follows the kit's value rule: Value (a pointer to your state) with OnValueChange controls it, DefaultValue starts an uncontrolled one. Value and DefaultValue choose the option whose Value equals them; when none does, or DefaultValue is nil, nothing is chosen and the placeholder shows. Both are pointers, so that the zero value of K (the int 0, say) can be an option: new(0) chooses it, nil chooses nothing.

Inside a [`Field`](#type-field) the trigger takes the field's id, so the label points to it and names it, the field's description or error describes it, and an error marks it invalid.

The list is a deviation from shadcn in one place: it always opens below (or above, when there is no room) the trigger, like shadcn's position="popper", where shadcn's default aligns the chosen option over the trigger; and it has no scroll buttons, since the list scrolls.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
var chosen string
page := kit.Select[string]{
    Placeholder: "Select a fruit",
    AriaLabel:   "Fruit",
    Items: []kit.SelectItem[string]{
        {Value: "apple", Label: "Apple"},
        {Value: "banana", Label: "Banana"},
    },
    OnValueChange: func(v string) { chosen = v },
}
app := telatest.Mount(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Select a fruit Fruit"))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("option", "Banana"))
fmt.Println("chose", chosen)
// Output: chose banana
```

#### func (Select[K]) Build

```go
func (s Select[K]) Build() tela.Node
```

Build returns the trigger and, in a portal, the list while it is open.

### type SelectItem

```go
type SelectItem[K comparable] struct {

    // reports.
```

### type Slider

```go
type Slider struct {
    // Value points to the value of a controlled one-knob slider; nil leaves
    // it to the slider, which starts at DefaultValue (Min when it is nil: a
    // pointer, so that 0 can be a start, as RadioGroup.DefaultValue is).
    // OnValueChange is called with the new value on every change.
    Value         *float64
    DefaultValue  *float64
    OnValueChange func(float64)
    // ValueSource is Value for a slider whose value is moved by something
    // other than the user, many times a second, such as a seek bar a clock
    // advances: it points to a tela.Value that holds the value, and the
    // knob and the range follow it by repainting, with no build of the
    // slider or its parent on each change. The slider is controlled by it:
    // OnValueChange must store the value the user asks for in it. It is read
    // when the slider builds (aria-valuenow), so a parent that builds from
    // time to time, say once a second, keeps the semantics current. It
    // takes the place of Value and DefaultValue; use it with one knob.
    ValueSource *tela.Value[float64]
    // Values, DefaultValues and OnValuesChange do the same for any number of
    // knobs (one per value, in ascending order): they take the place of
    // the three fields above when given.
    Values         *[]float64
    DefaultValues  []float64
    OnValuesChange func([]float64)
    // OnValueCommit is called with the values when the user stops changing
    // them: the pointer is released, or a key changed a value.
    OnValueCommit func([]float64)
    // Min and Max are the ends of the track: 0 and 100 by default.
    Min, Max float64
    // Step is the distance between the values the knobs can take (1 by
    // default).
    Step float64
    // MinStepsBetweenThumbs is the least number of Steps between two
    // knobs; 0 lets them touch.
    MinStepsBetweenThumbs int
    // Orientation is Horizontal (the default) or Vertical.
    Orientation Orientation
    // Direction is "ltr" or "rtl"; empty is the direction at the slider's
    // position (tela.UseDirection: the nearest h.Dir above it, left to right
    // without one). Under "rtl" a horizontal slider has its
    // Min at the right, ArrowLeft increases the value and a drag follows
    // the pointer; a Direction given here also sets the direction of the
    // slider's layout.
    Direction string
    // Disabled dims the slider and makes it ignore the user.
    Disabled bool
    // FormatValue returns a value as people read it (aria-valuetext).
    FormatValue func(float64) string
    // AriaLabel names the slider; ThumbLabels name each knob.
    AriaLabel   string
    ThumbLabels []string
    // Class is added after the recipe's classes. TrackClass, RangeClass and
    // ThumbClass do the same for their parts.
    Class      string
    TrackClass string
    RangeClass string
    ThumbClass string
    // Props are more props for the root element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

Slider picks a number, or a range, by dragging a knob along a track, shadcn/ui's Slider, on aria.UseSlider: a press on the track moves the nearest knob there and goes on dragging it, the arrow keys move the focused knob by Step (PageUp and PageDown by a tenth of the range, Home and End to its ends), and each knob is a slider with aria-valuenow. Dragging only repaints: the knob and the range follow the pointer without the component being built on every move.

With one knob, use Value, DefaultValue and OnValueChange, the kit's rule for a value:

```go
vol, setVol := tela.UseState(30.0)
kit.Slider{Value: &vol, OnValueChange: setVol.Set, Max: 100, Step: 5, AriaLabel: "Volume"}
```

An uncontrolled one starts where DefaultValue points (new(50.0) makes the pointer), and at Min without one, so that a slider from -50 to 50 can start at 0.

With several (a price range has two), the values are a slice, as in Radix and shadcn/ui, and the knobs never pass each other:

```go
kit.Slider{DefaultValues: []float64{20, 80}, ThumbLabels: []string{"Minimum price", "Maximum price"}}
```

A Vertical slider has its Min at the bottom and takes the height of its container (at least 11rem).

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
volume := 30.0
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("w-64 p-6"), kit.Slider{AriaLabel: "Volume", DefaultValue: &volume, Step: 10,
        OnValueChange: func(v float64) { volume = v }})
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Focus(telatest.ByRole("slider", "Volume"))
app.Press("ArrowRight")
fmt.Println("volume", volume)
// Output: volume 40
```


### type Style

```go
type Style struct {
    AlertDialog  AlertDialogStyle
    Avatar       AvatarStyle
    Badge        BadgeStyle
    Button       ButtonStyle
    Calendar     CalendarStyle
    Card         CardStyle
    Checkbox     CheckboxStyle
    ColorInput   ColorInputStyle
    ColorPicker  ColorPickerStyle
    ContextMenu  MenuStyle
    DatePicker   DatePickerStyle
    Dialog       DialogStyle
    DropdownMenu MenuStyle
    Field        FieldStyle
    FieldSet     FieldSetStyle
    Input        InputStyle
    Label        LabelStyle
    Menubar      MenubarStyle
    Popover      PopoverStyle
    Progress     ProgressStyle
    RadioGroup   RadioGroupStyle
    Select       SelectStyle
    Separator    SeparatorStyle
    Skeleton     SkeletonStyle
    Slider       SliderStyle
    Switch       SwitchStyle
    Table        TableStyle
    Tabs         TabsStyle
    Textarea     TextareaStyle
    Toast        ToastStyle
    Toggle       ToggleStyle
    ToggleGroup  ToggleGroupStyle
    Tooltip      TooltipStyle
}
```

Style holds the recipe of every component: the whole look of the kit as data (ADR-129, K17). [`DefaultStyle`](#func-defaultstyle) returns a copy of the defaults to edit, and [`StyleProvider`](#type-styleprovider) applies an edited one to a subtree.

A recipe is a struct of class strings. Its fields follow one rule:

- Root is the class of the component's root element, and is always there;
- one field per other part, named after the part: Header, Title, Description, Action, Content, Footer, Image, Fallback, Label, Error, Icon;
- Variants, Sizes (and Orientations where there are two) are maps from a [`Variant`](#type-variant), [`Size`](#type-size) or [`Orientation`](#type-orientation) to classes, so that new keys are new variants;
- a state a component can be in without a variable of its own (Disabled) is a string named after it.

The classes go on the element in the order Root, variant, size, state, then the Class field of the component, and Tela's last-wins rule makes the last one decide, so a recipe or an instance overrides what comes before with no merging.

Part names are public API; the strings are defaults and may change with the look.

#### func DefaultStyle

```go
func DefaultStyle() Style
```

DefaultStyle returns a copy of the default recipes: the maps are copied too, so editing the result never changes the defaults or the style of another caller.

```go
s := kit.DefaultStyle()
s.Card.Root += " backdrop-blur-xl"
s.Button.Variants["glass"] = "bg-white/10 text-white hover:bg-white/20"
kit.StyleProvider{Style: &s, Children: app}
```

#### func UseStyle

```go
func UseStyle() *Style
```

UseStyle returns the style the component is under: the nearest [`StyleProvider`](#type-styleprovider)'s, else the defaults. It is a hook. The result is shared: read it, and copy it with a recipe's own fields before changing anything; to make a style of your own start from [`DefaultStyle`](#func-defaultstyle).

The kit components call it; call it yourself to build components that follow the active style:

```go
func (b Banner) Build() tela.Node {
    s := kit.UseStyle()
    return h.Div(cls(s.Card.Root, "bg-accent"), b.Children)
}
```

### type StyleProvider

```go
type StyleProvider struct {
    Style    *Style
    Children tela.Component
}
```

StyleProvider gives Style to the kit components below it, in place of the defaults: the style of a subtree, like h.Scheme is its color scheme. Providers nest; the nearest one wins. A nil Style provides the defaults.

```go
s := kit.DefaultStyle()
s.Button.Variants["glass"] = "bg-white/10 text-white backdrop-blur hover:bg-white/20"
return kit.StyleProvider{Style: &s, Children: Dashboard{}}
```

Give it a style once, for example from tela.UseMemo or a package variable, and do not edit that style afterwards: the components below rebuild when the pointer changes, not when what it points to does.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
// A recipe is data: copy the defaults, add a variant, give the copy to
// a subtree.
style := kit.DefaultStyle()
style.Button.Variants["glass"] = "bg-white/10 text-white backdrop-blur hover:bg-white/20"
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Fragment(kit.StyleProvider{Style: &style, Children: h.Div(h.Class("bg-slate-900 p-6"),
        kit.Button{Variant: "glass", Children: h.Text("Glass")})})
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
fmt.Println(app.Count(telatest.ByClass("backdrop-blur")))
// Output: 1
```

#### func (StyleProvider) Build

```go
func (p StyleProvider) Build() tela.Node
```

Build provides the style to the children.

### type Switch

```go
type Switch struct {
    // Size is Default or Sm.
    Size Size
    // Checked points to the state of a controlled switch; nil leaves it to
    // the switch, which starts at DefaultChecked.
    Checked *bool
    // DefaultChecked is the initial state of an uncontrolled switch.
    DefaultChecked bool
    // OnCheckedChange is called with the next state when the user toggles
    // the switch. For a controlled switch it is how the change is asked
    // for.
    OnCheckedChange func(bool)
    // Disabled makes the switch inert and dims it.
    Disabled bool
    // Required marks the switch as one the user must turn on
    // (aria-required).
    Required bool
    // Invalid marks the value as wrong (aria-invalid). A [Field] with an
    // Error sets it on its control.
    Invalid bool
    // ID is the switch's id, for a [Label]'s For. Inside a [Field] it
    // defaults to the field's.
    ID string
    // AriaLabel names a switch that has no label of its own.
    AriaLabel string
    // Class is added after the recipe's classes; ThumbClass does the same
    // for the knob.
    Class      string
    ThumbClass string
    // Props are more props for the switch element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

Switch is an on/off control that slides, shadcn/ui's Switch, on aria.UseSwitch: a click or Space toggles it and it has the switch role and aria-checked. Its state follows the kit's rule: Checked and OnCheckedChange to keep it yourself, DefaultChecked to let the switch keep it.

```go
wifi, setWifi := tela.UseState(true)
kit.Switch{Checked: &wifi, OnCheckedChange: setWifi.Set, AriaLabel: "Wi-Fi"}

kit.Field{Orientation: kit.Horizontal, Label: "Airplane mode", Children: kit.Switch{Size: kit.Sm}}
```

The knob moves with a transition. A Size the active [`Style`](#type-style) does not define panics in dev mode with the closest one.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
wifi := true
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"),
        kit.Switch{AriaLabel: "Wi-Fi", DefaultChecked: wifi, OnCheckedChange: func(on bool) { wifi = on }})
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("switch", "Wi-Fi"))
fmt.Println("wifi", wifi)
// Output: wifi false
```


Build returns the switch element.

```go
type SwitchStyle struct {
```

### type Tab

```go
type Tab[K comparable] struct {
    // Value is the tab's key: what Tabs.Value holds and OnValueChange
    // reports.
    Value K
    // Label is the text of the tab; it names the tab for assistive
    // technologies and its panel.
    Label string
    // Icon is drawn before the label; the zero Icon draws nothing.
    Icon tela.Icon

    Disabled bool

}
```

### type Table

```go
type Table[T any] struct {
    // Rows are the data, in the order to show them when unsorted.
    Rows []T
    // RowKey returns a comparable key that is unique among Rows (an ID);
    // nil keys rows by position.
    RowKey func(row T) any
    // Columns are the table's columns, in order.
    Columns []Column[T]

    // Sort controls the sort (nil: the table keeps it), DefaultSort starts
    // an uncontrolled table sorted, and OnSortChange is called with the new
    // state when a header is pressed.
    Sort         *SortState
    DefaultSort  SortState
    OnSortChange func(SortState)

    // Selected tells whether a row is selected: the row gets the selected
    // look and aria-selected. Nil leaves the rows unselectable.
    Selected func(row T) bool

    // RowProps returns more props for the element of a body row, such as
    // h.AriaLabel, h.TestID or a handler (h.OnClick, h.OnKeyDown): what
    // Column.CellProps does for one cell, for the whole row. The row is a
    // display: contents element, which has no box of its own (see
    // [TableStyle]), and the engine treats it as the cells it holds: its
    // pointer and key handlers are called for events on any of its cells,
    // as events bubble through the tree, and a ref on it, h.Ref, reports
    // the bounds of its cells together. Classes on the row do not paint (it
    // has no box): style a row through the cells, with CellClass or Column.Class.
    RowProps func(row T) tela.Child

    // Caption is drawn below the rows, and names the table for assistive
    // technologies. AriaLabel names a table that has none.
    Caption   string
    AriaLabel string
    // Empty is drawn in a row of its own when there are no rows (shadcn's
    // "No results."). Nil draws the header alone.
    Empty tela.Component

    // SortIcon, SortAscIcon and SortDescIcon replace the arrows of a
    // sortable header that is unsorted, ascending and descending.
    SortIcon, SortAscIcon, SortDescIcon tela.Icon

    // Class is added after the recipe's Root classes. The other Class
    // fields do the same for their part: the grid, every header cell,
    // every body cell and the caption.
    Class        string
    TableClass   string
    HeadClass    string
    CellClass    string
    CaptionClass string
    // Props are more props for the root element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

Table is a data table, shadcn/ui's Table with the sorting and the sticky header and columns of its data-table and scroll examples, as a typed component: columns say how to draw a row, and rows are the data.

```go
kit.Table[Invoice]{
    Caption: "A list of your recent invoices.",
    Rows:    invoices,
    RowKey:  func(i Invoice) any { return i.ID },
    Columns: []kit.Column[Invoice]{
        {Header: "Invoice", Cell: func(i Invoice) tela.Node { return h.Text(i.ID) },
            Sort: func(a, b Invoice) int { return strings.Compare(a.ID, b.ID) }},
        {Header: "Status", Cell: func(i Invoice) tela.Node { return h.Text(i.Status) }},
        {Header: "Amount", Align: kit.AlignRight, Cell: func(i Invoice) tela.Node { return h.Text(i.Amount) },
            Sort: func(a, b Invoice) int { return cmp.Compare(a.Cents, b.Cents) }},
    },
}
```

##### Sorting

The header of a column with a Sort (or Sortable) is a button, so Tab reaches it and Enter and Space press it. Pressing it cycles the column through ascending, descending and unsorted, as TanStack Table (the engine of shadcn's data table) does by default, and pressing another column starts that one ascending; only one column is sorted at a time. The sorted header carries aria-sort and shows an arrow. The sort is stable: rows that compare equal keep their order in Rows (also when descending). Sorting follows ADR-101's value rule: Sort (a pointer to your state) controls it, DefaultSort sets the start and OnSortChange reports every change.

```go
sort, setSort := tela.UseState(kit.SortState{Column: "amount", Direction: kit.Descending})
kit.Table[Invoice]{Sort: &sort, OnSortChange: setSort.Set, ...}
```

##### Layout

The table is a CSS grid, one track per column from its Width. A column of Width "auto" (the default) is as wide as its widest cell and shares the space the container leaves; "1fr" columns divide it by weight, and "200px" ones keep their size. The header sticks to the top of the container, so a table in a container with a height (Class: "max-h-80") scrolls its rows under the header; columns with Sticky stay at the left when the table scrolls sideways.

Rows are keyed by RowKey, so the state of the components in a row's cells follows the row when the order changes. Without RowKey a row's key is its position in the sorted rows.

The look is the pinned shadcn commit's table, with the deviations in [`TableStyle`](#type-tablestyle). A table has no row selection or editing; Selected only styles the rows it names, with aria-selected.

**Example**

```go
package kit_test

import (
    "cmp"
    "fmt"
    "strings"

    "github.com/kuronosu/tela"
    "github.com/kuronosu/tela/h"
    "github.com/kuronosu/tela/kit"
    "github.com/kuronosu/tela/telatest"
)

// Invoice is the row type of ExampleTable.
type Invoice struct {
    ID, Status string
    Cents      int
}

func ExampleTable() {
    t := &exampleT{}
    defer t.close()
    invoices := []Invoice{{"INV001", "Paid", 25000}, {"INV002", "Pending", 15000}, {"INV003", "Unpaid", 35000}}
    page := func() tela.Node {
        return h.Div(h.Class("w-[420px] p-6"), kit.Table[Invoice]{
            Caption: "A list of your recent invoices.",
            Rows:    invoices,
            RowKey:  func(i Invoice) any { return i.ID },
            Columns: []kit.Column[Invoice]{
                {Header: "Invoice", Cell: func(i Invoice) tela.Node { return h.Text(i.ID) },
                    Sort: func(a, b Invoice) int { return strings.Compare(a.ID, b.ID) }},
                {Header: "Status", Cell: func(i Invoice) tela.Node { return h.Text(i.Status) }},
                {Header: "Amount", Align: kit.AlignRight,
                    Cell: func(i Invoice) tela.Node { return h.Text(fmt.Sprintf("$%.2f", float64(i.Cents)/100)) },
                    Sort: func(a, b Invoice) int { return cmp.Compare(a.Cents, b.Cents) }},
            },
        })
    }
    app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
    app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Amount")) // ascending
    app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Amount")) // descending
    app.Expect(telatest.ByRole("columnheader", "Amount"), telatest.Sort("descending"))
    app.ExpectAria(`
        - table "A list of your recent invoices.":
          - caption: A list of your recent invoices.
          - rowgroup:
            - row "Invoice Status Amount":
              - columnheader "Invoice":
                - button "Invoice"
              - columnheader "Status"
              - columnheader "Amount":
                - button "Amount"
          - rowgroup:
            - row "INV003 Unpaid $350.00":
              - cell "INV003"
              - cell "Unpaid"
              - cell "$350.00"
            - row "INV001 Paid $250.00":
              - cell "INV001"
              - cell "Paid"
              - cell "$250.00"
            - row "INV002 Pending $150.00":
              - cell "INV002"
              - cell "Pending"
              - cell "$150.00"
    `)
    fmt.Println("sorted by amount, largest first")
    // Output: sorted by amount, largest first
}
```

#### func (Table[T]) Build

```go
func (t Table[T]) Build() tela.Node
```

Build returns the table.

### type TableStyle

```go
type TableStyle struct {
    // Root is the scrolling container (shadcn's table-container). Give the
    // table a height with Class (max-h-96) to scroll it vertically with its
    // header kept in place.
    Root string
    // Table is the grid; the column tracks are added by the component.
    // It is as wide as its columns and at least as wide as the container,
    // so that a sticky column has a containing block as wide as the
    // scrolled content.
    Table string
    // Header, Body and Footer are the row groups (thead, tbody, tfoot) and
    // Row a row (tr); they have no box, so their classes are the inherited
    // ones: text color, font, and the `group` the cells' variants read.
    Header, Body, Footer, Row string
    // Head is a header cell (th) and Cell a body cell (td). Both are flex
    // containers that center their content vertically (`align-middle`). The
    // border under every row is here.
    Head, Cell string
    // CellWithLastRow is added to the cells of the last body row (shadcn's
    // [&_tr:last-child]:border-0).
    CellWithLastRow string
    // FooterCell is added to the footer's cells: its top border and
    // background.
    FooterCell string
    // Aligns are the classes of a column's alignment, by [ColumnAlign].
    Aligns map[ColumnAlign]string
    // HeadSticky is added to every header cell, which sticks to the top
    // of the scrolling container, over the rows that scroll under it; and
    // HeadStickyColumn to the header cell of a sticky column too.
    HeadSticky, HeadStickyColumn string
    // StickyColumn is added to the body cells of a sticky column, with an
    // opaque background so that the cells that scroll under it do not show;
    // StickyColumnHover keeps it opaque on a hovered row (a translucent
    // bg-muted/50 would show them), StickyColumnSelected on a selected
    // one and StickyColumnFooter in the footer.
    StickyColumn, StickyColumnHover, StickyColumnSelected, StickyColumnFooter string
    // Caption is the caption (shadcn's caption-bottom: below the rows).
    Caption string
    // Empty is added to the cell that holds the [Table]'s Empty content
    // when there are no rows.
    Empty string
    // SortButton is added to the classes of the button inside the header
    // of a sortable column, which is a ghost [Button] with the sort arrow
    // after the title, as in shadcn's data-table example. The header cell
    // is a `group` with aria-sort, for group-aria-[sort=ascending]: and
    // group-aria-[sort=descending]: classes.
    SortButton string
}
```

TableStyle is the recipe of [`Table`](#type-table) (shadcn/ui's Table, TableHeader, TableBody, TableFooter, TableRow, TableHead, TableCell and TableCaption).

shadcn's table is an HTML table; Tela has no table layout (ARCHITECTURE §10), so this one is a CSS grid whose rows are display: contents elements, as ARIA's table pattern allows: the cells are the grid's items and the rows, row groups and header exist for the semantics tree and for the classes the cells inherit. The classes shadcn puts on a row or a row group and that paint (a row's border, its hover and selected backgrounds, the footer's top border and background) are on the cells here, with the group-hover: and group-aria-selected: variants of the row, since a display: contents element has no box to paint.

### type Tabs

```go
type Tabs[K comparable] struct {
    // Tabs are the tabs, in order.
    Tabs []Tab[K]
    // Value points to the selected tab of a controlled Tabs; nil leaves
    // the selection to the component, which starts at DefaultValue.
    Value *K
    // DefaultValue points to the tab an uncontrolled Tabs starts on; the
    // first enabled tab when it is nil or not one of Tabs. It is a pointer
    // so that the zero value of K (the int 0, say) can be a tab:
    // new(0) selects it.
    DefaultValue *K
    // OnValueChange is called with the key of the tab the user selected. For
    // a controlled Tabs it is how the change is asked for.
    OnValueChange func(K)
    // Orientation is Horizontal (the zero value) or Vertical.
    Orientation Orientation
    // Variant is Default (the muted pill) or TabsLine.
    Variant Variant
    // Direction is "ltr" or "rtl"; empty is the direction at the component's
    // position (tela.UseDirection: the nearest h.Dir above it, left to right
    // without one). Under "rtl" ArrowLeft goes to the next tab and ArrowRight to the previous one; a Direction given here also
    // sets the direction of the layout.
    Direction string
    // ManualActivation makes the arrow keys only move the focus; Enter or
    // Space selects the focused tab. By default the focused tab is selected.
    ManualActivation bool
    // AriaLabel names the tab list.
    AriaLabel string
    // Indicator replaces the underline of the TabsLine variant (and adds
    // one to any other variant): it is drawn inside the selected tab only,
    // so it is mounted by the tab that gains the selection and unmounted by
    // the one that loses it, and a LayoutID on its element makes it slide
    // between the tabs (a shared element transition). Give it an element
    // that is positioned against the tab, such as
    // h.Div(h.LayoutID("underline"), h.Class("absolute inset-x-0 -bottom-px h-0.5 bg-primary")).
    Indicator tela.Component

    // Class is added after the recipe's Root classes; the other Class
    // fields do the same for their part.
    Class        string
    ListClass    string
    TriggerClass string
    ContentClass string
    // Props are more props for the root element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

Tabs is a tab list with its panels, shadcn/ui's Tabs: a strip of triggers and the content of the selected one. It is built on aria.UseTabs, so the arrow keys move between the tabs and select them, Home and End jump to the first and last, Tab moves from the selected tab to its panel, and disabled tabs are skipped.

```go
kit.Tabs[string]{
    DefaultValue: new("account"),
    Tabs: []kit.Tab[string]{
        {Value: "account", Label: "Account", Content: AccountForm{}},
        {Value: "password", Label: "Password", Content: PasswordForm{}},
    },
}
```

The selected tab follows the kit's value rule: Value (a pointer to your state) with OnValueChange controls it, DefaultValue starts an uncontrolled one. There is always one selected tab: the first enabled one when no value is given, or the given one is missing or disabled.

Orientation Vertical lays the list out as a column beside the panel and moves with the up and down arrows. Variant TabsLine draws no pill and underlines the selected tab.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := kit.Tabs[string]{
    DefaultValue: new("account"),
    Tabs: []kit.Tab[string]{
        {Value: "account", Label: "Account", Content: h.Text("Make changes to your account.")},
        {Value: "password", Label: "Password", Content: h.Text("Change your password.")},
    },
}
app := telatest.Mount(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("tab", "Password"))
app.ExpectText("Change your password.")
fmt.Println("password tab shown")
// Output: password tab shown
```

#### func (Tabs[K]) Build

```go
func (t Tabs[K]) Build() tela.Node
```

Build returns the tabs element: the list of triggers and the selected panel.

### type TabsStyle

```go
type TabsStyle struct {
    // Root is the arrangement of the list and the panel.
    Root string
    // Orientations are the root's classes per orientation: Horizontal puts
    // the list above the panel, Vertical beside it.
    Orientations map[Orientation]string
    // List is the strip of triggers.
    List string
    // ListVariants are the looks of the list: Default (a muted pill) and
    // TabsLine (no background).
    ListVariants map[Variant]string
    // ListOrientations are the list's dimensions per orientation.
    ListOrientations map[Orientation]string
    // Trigger is what every tab has; its selected look is the aria-selected:
    // classes, and TriggerVariants (the list's variant) go after them.
    Trigger string
    // TriggerVariants are the classes a tab adds per variant of its list,
    // after Trigger (shadcn's group-data-[variant=…]/tabs-list:).
    TriggerVariants map[Variant]string
    // TriggerOrientations are the tab's classes per orientation (the
    // vertical list's tabs are full-width and start-aligned).
    TriggerOrientations map[Orientation]string
    // Icon is what a tab's icon has.
    Icon string
    // Indicator is the underline of the TabsLine list's selected tab (the
    // pseudo-element shadcn draws with after:, here a real element);
    // IndicatorOrientations place it per orientation.
    Indicator             string
    IndicatorOrientations map[Orientation]string
    // Content is the panel.
    Content string
}
```

TabsStyle is the recipe of [`Tabs`](#type-tabs) (shadcn/ui's Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger and TabsContent).

### type Textarea

```go
type Textarea struct {
    // Value points to the text of a controlled field; nil leaves the text
    // to the field, which starts with DefaultValue.
    Value        *string
    DefaultValue string
    // OnValueChange is called with the new text after every edit.
    OnValueChange func(string)
    Placeholder   string
    Name          string
    // ID is the field's id, for a [Label]'s For. Inside a [Field] it
    // defaults to the field's.
    ID string
    // AriaLabel names a field that has no label of its own (see [Input]).
    AriaLabel string
    // Rows is the number of lines the field is tall (h.Rows); 0 leaves the
    // recipe's minimum height and the text to size it.
    Rows     int
    Disabled bool
    ReadOnly bool
    // Invalid marks the value as wrong (see [Input]); a [Field] with an
    // Error sets it.
    Invalid   bool
    AutoFocus bool
    MaxLength int
    // Class is added after the recipe's classes.
    Class string
    // Props are more props for the textarea element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

Textarea is a multi-line text field, shadcn/ui's Textarea. It grows with its text (field-sizing-content) from a minimum height of 64 px, and scrolls once a max-h-\* class in Class caps it. Its value follows the same rule as [`Input`](#type-input)'s.

```go
kit.Textarea{Placeholder: "Write a message", Value: &msg, OnValueChange: setMsg.Set}
```
