### type ToastHandle

```go
type ToastHandle struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

ToastHandle shows and dismisses the toasts of the [`Toaster`](#type-toaster) above the component that called [`UseToast`](#func-usetoast). It is a small comparable value, so it can sit in a struct component's fields without making it rebuild, and every method is safe from any goroutine: an HTTP callback or a worker can call Success when it is done.

#### func UseToast

```go
func UseToast() ToastHandle
```

UseToast returns the handle of the nearest [`Toaster`](#type-toaster) above the component. It is a hook. It panics when there is none: put kit.Toaster{Children: …} around the app, once.

```go
func Save() tela.Node {
    toast := kit.UseToast()
    return kit.Button{OnClick: func() {
        toast.Success("Saved", kit.ToastDescription("Your changes are live."))
    }, Children: h.Text("Save")}
}
```

#### func (ToastHandle) Dismiss

```go
func (t ToastHandle) Dismiss(id ToastID)
```

Dismiss closes the toast with the id; an id that is gone is ignored.

#### func (ToastHandle) DismissAll

```go
func (t ToastHandle) DismissAll()
```

DismissAll closes every toast.

#### func (ToastHandle) Error

```go
func (t ToastHandle) Error(title string, opts ...ToastOption) ToastID
```

Error shows a toast with an error icon. It is announced as an alert.

#### func (ToastHandle) Info

```go
func (t ToastHandle) Info(title string, opts ...ToastOption) ToastID
```

Info shows a toast with an info icon.

#### func (ToastHandle) Loading

```go
func (t ToastHandle) Loading(title string, opts ...ToastOption) ToastID
```

Loading shows a toast with a spinner that stays until it is dismissed or replaced (see [`ToastReplace`](#func-toastreplace)).

```go
id := toast.Loading("Uploading…")
// … later, from any goroutine:
toast.Success("Uploaded", kit.ToastReplace(id))
```

#### func (ToastHandle) Show

```go
func (t ToastHandle) Show(title string, opts ...ToastOption) ToastID
```

Show shows a toast with the title and returns its id. It is safe from any goroutine.

```go
id := toast.Show("Event created", kit.ToastDescription("Sunday at 9:00 AM"),
    kit.ToastAction("Undo", undo))
```

#### func (ToastHandle) Success

```go
func (t ToastHandle) Success(title string, opts ...ToastOption) ToastID
```

Success shows a toast with a check icon.

#### func (ToastHandle) Warning

```go
func (t ToastHandle) Warning(title string, opts ...ToastOption) ToastID
```

Warning shows a toast with a warning icon.

### type ToastID

```go
type ToastID uint64
```

ToastID names one toast of a [`Toaster`](#type-toaster): [`ToastHandle`](#type-toasthandle).Show returns it, and Dismiss and [`ToastReplace`](#func-toastreplace) take it.

### type ToastIcons

```go
type ToastIcons struct {
    Success, Info, Warning, Error, Loading tela.Icon
}
```

ToastIcons are the icons of the toast kinds; a zero Icon keeps shadcn's.

### type ToastOption

```go
type ToastOption func(*toastData)
```

ToastOption customizes a toast shown with [`ToastHandle`](#type-toasthandle).Show and its variants.

#### func ToastAction

```go
func ToastAction(label string, onClick func()) ToastOption
```

ToastAction adds a button to the toast. Clicking it calls onClick and dismisses the toast.

#### func ToastDescription

```go
func ToastDescription(text string) ToastOption
```

ToastDescription adds a second, lighter line under the title.

#### func ToastDuration

```go
func ToastDuration(d time.Duration) ToastOption
```

ToastDuration sets how long the toast stays: after it the toast is dismissed. [`ToastForever`](#constants) keeps it until it is dismissed by hand. The default is the Toaster's Duration (4 seconds), and a loading toast never closes by itself. The time is the window's frame clock, so it stops while the pointer rests over the toasts.

#### func ToastOnAutoClose

```go
func ToastOnAutoClose(f func()) ToastOption
```

ToastOnAutoClose calls f, on the UI thread, when the toast closes because its time ran out.

#### func ToastOnDismiss

```go
func ToastOnDismiss(f func()) ToastOption
```

ToastOnDismiss calls f, on the UI thread, when the toast is dismissed by the user or by [`ToastHandle`](#type-toasthandle).Dismiss.

#### func ToastReplace

```go
func ToastReplace(id ToastID) ToastOption
```

ToastReplace makes the toast replace the one with this id, in the same place and with its timer restarted, as sonner's id option does: a loading toast becomes a success or an error when the work is over. When no toast has the id, a new one is shown.

### type ToastPosition

```go
type ToastPosition string
```

ToastPosition is the corner or edge of the window a [`Toaster`](#type-toaster) puts its toasts at. The zero value is ToastBottomRight. Left and right are the window's, whatever the direction, as sonner's positions are (the toast's own layout, its icon, action and close button, follows the direction).

```go
const (
    ToastTopLeft      ToastPosition = "top-left"
    ToastTopCenter    ToastPosition = "top-center"
    ToastTopRight     ToastPosition = "top-right"
    ToastBottomLeft   ToastPosition = "bottom-left"
    ToastBottomCenter ToastPosition = "bottom-center"
    ToastBottomRight  ToastPosition = "bottom-right"
)
```

### type ToastStyle

```go
type ToastStyle struct {
    // Root is the viewport, Fixed or Inline is added to it (the viewport is
    // fixed to the window, or absolute inside the nearest positioned
    // ancestor for an Inline Toaster) and Positions say where.
    Root, Fixed, Inline string
    Positions           map[ToastPosition]string
    // Item is one toast: all of them are absolute at the viewport's edge, and
    // the Toaster moves them with a translation and a scale. Sides add the
    // edge ("top" or "bottom") and x the side they are laid against.
    Item  string
    Sides map[string]string
    // Enter and Exit are the classes an entering toast starts from and an
    // exiting one goes to, per edge.
    Enter, Exit map[string]string
    // Hidden is added to the toasts beyond VisibleToasts.
    Hidden string
    // Body is the row inside a toast that holds the icon, the text and the
    // action; Collapsed is added to the body of a toast behind the first
    // while the stack is collapsed (its content is invisible, only its card
    // peeks out).
    Body, Collapsed string
    // Bridge is the invisible strip above an expanded toast that keeps the
    // pointer over the viewport while it crosses the gap between two toasts
    // (sonner's ::after).
    Bridge string
    // Icon is the box of a toast's icon, IconSvg the drawing, and Spinner is
    // added to the loading icon.
    Icon, IconSvg, Spinner string
    Content                string
    Title                  string
    Description            string
    // Action is the toast's button, Close the round button of a Toaster
    // with a CloseButton and CloseIcon its icon.
    Action, Close, CloseIcon string
}
```

ToastStyle is the recipe of [`Toaster`](#type-toaster) (shadcn/ui's Sonner wrapper over sonner's default styles, sonner 2.x). The root element of a Toaster is its viewport: the box at the edge of the window the toasts stack in.

### type Toaster

```go
type Toaster struct {
    // Position is where the toasts stack: ToastBottomRight (the zero
    // value), ToastBottomLeft, ToastBottomCenter, ToastTopRight,
    // ToastTopLeft or ToastTopCenter.
    Position ToastPosition
    // Duration is how long a toast stays by default, 4 seconds when zero;
    // ToastForever keeps toasts until they are dismissed.
    Duration time.Duration
    // VisibleToasts is how many toasts show at once, 3 when zero.
    VisibleToasts int
    // Expand keeps the stack fanned out, as when the pointer is over it.
    Expand bool
    // CloseButton gives every toast a close button.
    CloseButton bool
    // Inline draws the toasts inside the nearest positioned ancestor of the
    // Toaster instead of in a layer fixed to the window: a toaster for a
    // panel or a preview. The position classes then place it in that box.
    Inline bool
    // Icons replace the icons of the kinds; CloseIcon the one of the close
    // button.
    Icons     ToastIcons
    CloseIcon tela.Icon
    // Children is the app: the components below that call UseToast.
    Children tela.Component

    // Class is added after the recipe's Root classes (the viewport's);
    // ToastClass is added to every toast.
    Class      string
    ToastClass string
    // Props are more props for the viewport element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

Toaster shows the toasts of its app: shadcn/ui's Sonner. It goes once, around the app, and the components below it show toasts with a handle from [`UseToast`](#func-usetoast):

```go
tela.Main(tela.App{Title: "Notes", Root: kit.Toaster{Children: Notes{}}, Theme: &theme})

toast := kit.UseToast()
toast.Success("Saved")
```

The toasts stack at a corner of the window (Position; bottom right by default). The newest is in front, with the ones before it peeking out behind it, scaled down; at most VisibleToasts (3) show. While the pointer is over the toasts they fan out to show each in full and their timers stop, and they go on from where they were when it leaves, as sonner does. A toast closes by itself after its Duration, 4 seconds by default; the clock is the window's frame clock, so telatest's Advance moves it and an app with only a waiting toast wakes up no more often than every 100 ms. Toasts enter and leave sliding from the edge of the window.

Toasts are announced to assistive technologies: each is a "status" and an error an "alert".

Compared with sonner: there is no swipe to dismiss, no promise helper (show a Loading toast and replace it), no rich colors, and the toasts do not change layout on narrow windows.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
// The Toaster goes once around the app; any component below it shows
// toasts with the handle of kit.UseToast.
app := telatest.Mount(t, kit.Toaster{Children: seedOnClick{}})
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Save"))
app.ExpectText("Your changes are live.")
fmt.Println("toast shown")
// Output: toast shown
```

#### func (Toaster) Build

```go
func (t Toaster) Build() tela.Node
```

Build returns the app and the viewport that shows the toasts.

### type Toggle

```go
type Toggle struct {
    // Variant is Default or Outline.
    Variant Variant
    // Size is Default, Sm or Lg.
    Size Size
    // Pressed points to the state of a controlled toggle; nil leaves it to
    // the toggle, which starts at DefaultPressed.
    Pressed *bool
    // DefaultPressed is the initial state of an uncontrolled toggle.
    DefaultPressed bool
    // OnPressedChange is called with the next state when the user toggles
    // the button. For a controlled toggle it is how the change is asked
    // for.
    OnPressedChange func(bool)
    // Disabled makes the toggle inert and dims it.
    Disabled bool
    // Invalid marks the value as wrong (aria-invalid).
    Invalid bool
    // AriaLabel names a toggle whose content is not text.
    AriaLabel string
    // Icon is drawn before the children.
    Icon tela.Icon
    // Children is the label.
    Children tela.Component
    // Class is added after the recipe's classes.
    Class string
    // Props are more props for the button element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

Toggle is a button that stays pressed, shadcn/ui's Toggle, on aria.UseToggleButton: a click, Enter or Space turns it on and off, and it has aria-pressed. Its state follows the kit's rule: Pressed and OnPressedChange to keep it yourself, DefaultPressed to let the toggle keep it.

```go
bold, setBold := tela.UseState(false)
kit.Toggle{Variant: kit.Outline, Pressed: &bold, OnPressedChange: setBold.Set,
    Icon: lucide.Bold, AriaLabel: "Bold"}
```

For a row of toggles that share a choice, see [`ToggleGroup`](#type-togglegroup). A Variant or Size the active [`Style`](#type-style) does not define panics in dev mode with the closest one.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
bold := false
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"), kit.Toggle{Variant: kit.Outline, Icon: iconBold, AriaLabel: "Bold",
        OnPressedChange: func(on bool) { bold = on }})
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Bold"))
fmt.Println("bold", bold)
// Output: bold true
```

#### func (Toggle) Build

```go
func (t Toggle) Build() tela.Node
```

Build returns the toggle element.

### type ToggleGroup

```go
type ToggleGroup[K comparable] struct {
    // Items are the buttons, in order.
    Items []ToggleGroupItem[K]
    // Variant (Default or Outline) and Size (Default, Sm or Lg) are the
    // toggle looks of every item.
    Variant Variant
    Size    Size
    // Spacing is the space between items, in steps of 4 px. 0 joins the
    // items into one segmented bar (shadcn's default).
    Spacing int
    // Multiple lets any number of items be on.
    Multiple bool
    // Value points to the key that is on in a controlled single-choice
    // group; nil leaves it to the group, which starts at DefaultValue (nil:
    // none on). OnValueChange is called with the key that has just been
    // turned on.
    Value         *K
    DefaultValue  *K
    OnValueChange func(K)
    // Selected is the selection of a controlled group, DefaultSelected the
    // starting one of an uncontrolled group and OnSelectionChange is called
    // with the next selection. The zero aria.Selection leaves the selection
    // to the group.
    Selected          aria.Selection[K]
    DefaultSelected   aria.Selection[K]
    OnSelectionChange func(aria.Selection[K])
    // DisallowEmptySelection keeps one item on: pressing the only item that
    // is on does nothing.
    DisallowEmptySelection bool
    // Orientation is Horizontal (the default) or Vertical, which the arrow
    // keys follow; the items are laid out in a row either way (use Class
    // "flex-col" for a column).
    Orientation Orientation
    // Direction is "ltr" or "rtl"; empty is the direction at the component's
    // position (tela.UseDirection: the nearest h.Dir above it, left to right
    // without one). Under "rtl" ArrowLeft goes to the next item and ArrowRight to the previous one; a Direction given here also
    // sets the direction of the layout.
    Direction string
    // Disabled disables every item.
    Disabled bool
    // AriaLabel names the group; without it a [FieldSet]'s legend does.
    AriaLabel string
    // Class is added after the recipe's classes; ItemClass is added to every
    // item.
    Class     string
    ItemClass string
    // Props are more props for the group element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

ToggleGroup is a row of toggle buttons that share a choice, shadcn/ui's ToggleGroup, on aria.UseToggleGroup: the segmented control, and a formatting toolbar. With one choice (the default) the group is a radio group of toggle buttons; with Multiple any number of items are on and the group is a toolbar. The group is one tab stop: the arrows move the focus between the items, Home and End jump, and Enter or Space turns an item on or off.

A single-choice group follows the kit's value rule with Value (a pointer to a key), DefaultValue and OnValueChange; pressing the item that is on turns it off unless DisallowEmptySelection, which a segmented control sets:

```go
view, setView := tela.UseState("list")
kit.ToggleGroup[string]{
    Value: &view, OnValueChange: setView.Set, DisallowEmptySelection: true, AriaLabel: "View",
    Items: []kit.ToggleGroupItem[string]{
        {Value: "list", Label: "List"},
        {Value: "grid", Label: "Grid"},
    },
}
```

A group with Multiple holds an [`aria.Selection`](API-Reference-aria#type-selection) instead, with Selected, DefaultSelected and OnSelectionChange:

```go
kit.ToggleGroup[string]{Multiple: true, Variant: kit.Outline, DefaultSelected: aria.SelectionOf("bold"),
    Items: []kit.ToggleGroupItem[string]{{Value: "bold", Icon: lucide.Bold, AriaLabel: "Bold"}, ...}}
```

Selected, DefaultSelected and OnSelectionChange also work on a single-choice group, for a controlled group that may have no item on.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
theme := "system"
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"), kit.ToggleGroup[string]{
        AriaLabel: "Theme", Variant: kit.Outline, DefaultValue: &theme, DisallowEmptySelection: true,
        OnValueChange: func(k string) { theme = k },
        Items: []kit.ToggleGroupItem[string]{
            {Value: "light", Label: "Light"}, {Value: "dark", Label: "Dark"}, {Value: "system", Label: "System"},
        }})
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("radio", "Dark"))
fmt.Println("theme", theme)
// Output: theme dark
```

#### func (ToggleGroup[K]) Build

```go
func (g ToggleGroup[K]) Build() tela.Node
```

Build returns the group element.

### type ToggleGroupItem

```go
type ToggleGroupItem[K comparable] struct {
    // Value is the item's key, what the group's selection holds.
    Value K
    // Label is the item's text.
    Label string
    // Icon is drawn before the label; give an AriaLabel to an item that has
    // only an icon.
    Icon tela.Icon
    // Children replaces the Label with any content.
    Children tela.Component
    // AriaLabel names an item whose content is not text.
    AriaLabel string
    // Disabled makes the item inert and dims it.
    Disabled bool
}
```

ToggleGroupItem is one item of a [`ToggleGroup`](#type-togglegroup): a toggle button with an icon, a label, or both.

### type ToggleGroupStyle

```go
type ToggleGroupStyle struct {
    // Root is the row that holds the items (shadcn's group/toggle-group class is
    // left out: Tela has no named groups, and nothing selects on it).
    Root string
    // Item is added to the toggle classes of every item.
    Item string
    // ItemWithoutSpacing is added to an item of a group with no space
    // between its items (shadcn's data-[spacing=0]:): square corners except
    // the ends, no shadow.
    ItemWithoutSpacing string
    // OutlineItemWithoutSpacing is added to an Outline item of a group with
    // no space between its items: one border between neighbors.
    OutlineItemWithoutSpacing string
}
```

ToggleGroupStyle is the recipe of [`ToggleGroup`](#type-togglegroup) (shadcn/ui's ToggleGroup and ToggleGroupItem). The look of an item comes from [`ToggleStyle`](#type-togglestyle): its Root, the group's Variant and Size, and On.

### type ToggleStyle

```go
type ToggleStyle struct {
    // Root is what every toggle has: layout, text, hover, focus ring,
    // disabled and invalid. The unconditional classes (bg-transparent, the
    // border color) come before the conditional ones, as Tela's last-wins
    // order needs where CSS has the variant order.
    Root string
    // Variants are the looks: Default and Outline.
    Variants map[Variant]string
    // Sizes are the dimensions: the default, Sm and Lg.
    Sizes map[Size]string
    // On is added while the toggle is on (shadcn's
    // data-[state=on]:), after the variant, so that it wins over hover.
    // The toggle button is aria-pressed and the item of a single-selection
    // group aria-checked, so it styles both.
    On string
    // Icon is what the icon slot has (shadcn's [&_svg]: classes).
    Icon string
}
```

ToggleStyle is the recipe of [`Toggle`](#type-toggle) (shadcn/ui's toggleVariants), which the items of a [`ToggleGroup`](#type-togglegroup) use too.

### type Tooltip

```go
type Tooltip struct {
    // Trigger is the element the tooltip is about.
    Trigger Trigger
    // Content is what the tooltip says: text, or a short component.
    Content tela.Component
    // Placement is the side of the trigger the tooltip is on: "top" (the
    // default), "bottom", "left" or "right"; a Floating UI placement such as
    // "top-start" also works. Align is where it sits along that side:
    // "start", "center" (the default) or "end". The tooltip flips to the
    // other side when there is no room.
    Placement, Align string
    // Offset is the distance in pixels between the trigger and the tooltip
    // (zero by default: the arrow touches the trigger).
    Offset float32
    // Delay is how long the pointer must rest on the trigger before the
    // tooltip opens. Zero opens it at once, as shadcn's provider does.
    // Keyboard focus never waits.
    Delay time.Duration
    // Disabled keeps the tooltip from opening.
    Disabled bool

    // Open points to the open state of a controlled tooltip; nil leaves the
    // state to the tooltip, which starts closed unless DefaultOpen is set.
    Open         *bool
    DefaultOpen  bool
    OnOpenChange func(open bool)

    // Class is added after the recipe's Root classes, to the tooltip;
    // ArrowClass does the same for the arrow.
    Class      string
    ArrowClass string
    // Props are more props for the tooltip element.
    Props tela.Child
}
```

Tooltip is a small label that explains its trigger, shadcn/ui's Tooltip: it appears when the pointer rests on the trigger or the keyboard focuses it, points at it with an arrow, and goes away when the pointer leaves, a key is pressed, the trigger is pressed or Escape is. The trigger is described by it (aria-describedby), so assistive technologies read it after the trigger's own name.

```go
kit.Tooltip{
    Trigger: kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Size: kit.Icon, AriaLabel: "Add", Icon: plus},
    Content: h.Text("Add to library"),
}
```

The Trigger slot is a [`Trigger`](#type-trigger). The tooltips of a window are a group, as in shadcn's TooltipProvider and React Aria: only one is open, and once one has opened, moving to another trigger shows its tooltip at once, whatever its Delay; there is nothing to wrap them in.

A tooltip is for elements that already have a name and a tab stop; it should hold text, never controls. The tooltip exists only while it is open. Open, DefaultOpen and OnOpenChange are the usual controlled and uncontrolled pair.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"), kit.Tooltip{
        Trigger: kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Size: kit.Icon, AriaLabel: "Add", Children: h.Text("+")},
        Content: h.Text("Add to library"),
    })
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page, telatest.NoSettle())
app.Hover(telatest.ByRole("button", "Add"))
fmt.Println("tooltip:", app.Count(telatest.ByRole("tooltip", "Add to library")) == 1)
app.MouseMove(300, 300)
app.Advance(time.Second)
fmt.Println("tooltip:", app.Count(telatest.ByRole("tooltip", "Add to library")) == 1)
// Output:
// tooltip: true
// tooltip: false
```

#### func (Tooltip) Build

```go
func (t Tooltip) Build() tela.Node
```

Build returns the trigger and the tooltip's portal.

### type TooltipStyle

```go
type TooltipStyle struct {
    // Root is the tooltip: the foreground color as background, small text
    // and the entrance.
    Root string
    // Exit is what the tooltip transitions to as it closes.
    Exit string
    // Sides adds classes for the side of the trigger the tooltip is on
    // ("top", "right", "bottom" or "left"): the transform origin of the
    // entrance and the slide of 0.5rem it starts from.
    Sides map[string]string
    // Arrow is the arrow: a square turned 45 degrees, half under the
    // tooltip. ArrowSides adds, per side, the margin that sinks it 2 px
    // into the tooltip (shadcn's translate-y-[calc(-50%_-_2px)]); Floating
    // UI puts the arrow's center on the edge.
    Arrow      string
    ArrowSides map[string]string
}
```

TooltipStyle is the recipe of [`Tooltip`](#type-tooltip) (shadcn/ui's TooltipContent and its arrow).

### type Trigger

```go
type Trigger interface {
    // WithTriggerProps returns the component with p applied to its root
    // element, after the props the component sets itself, so that p's
    // handlers run along with the component's own.
    WithTriggerProps(p tela.Prop) tela.Component
}
```

Trigger is what a trigger slot takes: the Trigger field of [`Dialog`](#type-dialog), [`AlertDialog`](#type-alertdialog), [`Popover`](#type-popover) and [`Tooltip`](#type-tooltip), and of the menus, selects and pickers that open something. It is a component whose root element can receive the props of a trigger: the press that opens the overlay, the aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and aria-controls that say what it does, the ref the overlay is placed against, the hover and focus handlers of a tooltip. The overlay builds those props with its aria hook and calls WithTriggerProps to put them on the trigger.

One rule holds for every trigger slot of the kit:

- a kit component that can be a trigger implements Trigger, and [`Button`](#type-button) does: Trigger: kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Children: h.Text("Open")};
- a component of your own implements it with one method, merging p into the props of its root element (the way a kit component merges it with its Props field);
- anything else, an element or a function component, is made a Trigger with [`TriggerFunc`](#type-triggerfunc), which receives the props and puts them on the element it chooses.

A Trigger is the equivalent of Radix's asChild: the overlay does not wrap the trigger in an element of its own, so the button you wrote is the one the screen reader finds, with its name and its tab stop.

### type TriggerFunc

```go
type TriggerFunc func(p tela.Prop) tela.Node
```

TriggerFunc makes a function a [`Trigger`](#type-trigger): it is given the props of the trigger and returns the element that carries them. Use it for a trigger that is not a kit component, such as an avatar or a link:

```go
kit.Popover{
    Trigger: kit.TriggerFunc(func(p tela.Prop) tela.Node {
        return h.Button(p, cls("rounded-full"), kit.Avatar{Fallback: "AB"})
    }),
    Children: profile,
}
```

The function runs as a component of its own, so it may use hooks. The props make the element a button that can be pressed and focused; give a different role with h.Role after p when the element is something else.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
// Any element can be a trigger: it is given the props and puts them
// where it wants.
page := func() tela.Node {
    return h.Div(h.Class("p-6"), kit.Popover{
        Trigger: kit.TriggerFunc(func(p tela.Prop) tela.Node {
            return h.Button(p, h.Class("rounded-full"), h.AriaLabel("Account"), kit.Avatar{Fallback: "AB"})
        }),
        AriaLabel: "Account",
        Children:  h.P(h.Text("Signed in as Ana.")),
    })
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Account"))
fmt.Println("open:", app.Count(telatest.ByRole("dialog", "Account")) == 1)
// Output: open: true
```

#### func (TriggerFunc) WithTriggerProps

```go
func (f TriggerFunc) WithTriggerProps(p tela.Prop) tela.Component
```

WithTriggerProps returns the component that calls f with p.

### type Variant

```go
type Variant string
```

Variant is the look of a component among the ones its recipe defines: a Button is Default, Secondary, Outline, Ghost, Destructive or Link. The constants are shared by the components that have the same variants; an app defines its own by adding a name to a recipe's Variants map (s.Button.Variants\["glass"\] = "...") and using Variant("glass").

```go
const (
    Default     Variant = ""
    Secondary   Variant = "secondary"
    Outline     Variant = "outline"
    Ghost       Variant = "ghost"
    Destructive Variant = "destructive"
    Link        Variant = "link"
)
```

The variants shadcn/ui's components share. Default is the zero value, so leaving Variant out gives the default look.

```go
const TabsLine Variant = "line"
```

TabsLine is the Variant of a [`Tabs`](#type-tabs) list that draws no background and underlines the selected tab (shadcn's tabsListVariants "line"). The other variant, Default, is the muted pill.
